input.prompt:
Design the ENGINE layer for a new feature in /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp. Do not write code files — return a detailed implementation plan with concrete file paths, type/method signatures, and sequencing.

## Feature
A new 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector needs this data + actions:
- List of branches (git) / bookmarks (jj) for a workroom, so the user can pick one and switch to it.
- Current branch (already available).
- Ahead/behind counts vs the upstream/origin tracking ref.
- Last-fetch timestamp ("last fetched 9 minutes ago").
- Actions: fetch, push to origin, pull from origin with rebase, switch branch.

## Established facts from exploration (trust these)

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16` — `VCSProviding` protocol, 8 requirements, all READ-ONLY, no branch listing, no mutation, no network. Two defaulted members at `:55-64` (`commitParentFileContent`, `workingBaseFileContent` default to nil) — precedent for adding defaulted members so existing stub conformers in tests don't all break.
`VCSProviding.swift:67` — `enum VCS` with `repoKind(at:)` (`:70`) and `provider(for:)` (`:87`) routing `jj*` → `RustJJProvider`, `plainGit` → `GitProvider`.

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitProvider.swift:17` — `struct GitProvider: VCSProviding`, SwiftGitX 0.4.0. Has a NON-protocol `func workingStatus(root:) throws -> GitWorkingStatus` at `:271`; `GitProvider.swift:466-477` has a comment saying the Git-shaped working status "unifies onto a shared VCSProviding.workingStatus in the follow-on".
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/RustJJProvider.swift:6` — `struct RustJJProvider: VCSProviding`, `import WrVcs` (UniFFI). Non-protocol `workingStatus(root:) throws -> WorkroomStatus` at `:70`. Private `static func run(_ exe:_ args:cwd:timeout:) async throws -> String` at `:232` shells `jj` via `StatusCommandRunner` for 4 things jj-lib doesn't expose well.

CRITICAL AUTH FINDING: SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass NULL for the options struct (`Repository+fetch.swift:30-32`, `Repository+push.swift:49-51`) so there is ZERO credential support — HTTPS auth is impossible through it; `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). SwiftGitX's LOCAL ops are fine: `branch.list(_ type:) throws -> [Branch]` (`Collections/BranchCollection.swift:87`), `branch.local`/`.remote` sequences, `branch.current`, `switch(to: Branch)` (`Repository+switch.swift:33`, auto-creates a local tracking branch for a remote branch via `createTrackingBranch`), `remote.list()`.

Precedent for shelling out to network-touching binaries: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift` already runs `gh` for CI/PR data (`:194`, `:209`, `:249`, `:278`, `:295`) INCLUDING a mutating helper `runPRCommand(_ arguments:in:) -> CommandResult` at `:405`, and `gh auth status` at `:426` with `classifyGitHubCLI` at `:425-444` (exit 127 ⇒ not installed, timeout ⇒ don't cry wolf). It also already shells `git` at `:379` (`rev-parse HEAD`) and `:394` (`symbolic-ref`), with `static let gitHardening = ["-c", "core.fsmonitor="]` at `:63`. `FileTree.swift:162` shells `git ls-files`.
`static func ghProbeDirectory(path:vcs:projectRoot:)` at `:364-366` returns `vcs == "jj" ? projectRoot : path` — a jj workspace has no `.git`, so network commands must run from the colocated project root. Any new network op needs the same rule.

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift` — `protocol StatusCommandRunning` (`:24`) with `func run(_ executable:_ args:in directory:timeout:) async -> CommandResult`; `CommandResult` (`:9`) has `stdout/stderr/exitCode/timedOut/ok`, sentinels `commandNotFound = 127`, `gitFatal = 128`. Launches via `/usr/bin/env` (`:45`), PATH from `ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:49-57`), and sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` + `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` unconditionally (also in `ShellEnvironment.appOverrides`, `ShellEnvironment.swift:146-149`). Three-layer timeout: SIGTERM at +timeout, SIGKILL tree at +timeout+2, bounded 2s drain.
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/Timeout.swift:65` — `runBlocking(qos:_:)` GCD helper; `:21` `withTimeout(seconds:_:)`. Blocking libgit2/jj-lib reads MUST use `runBlocking`, never the cooperative pool (a past bug: "History pane loads forever").
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/JJSnapshotGate.swift:39` — `actor JJSnapshotGate`, `.shared`, `run<T>(projectRoot:_:)`, serializes MUTATING jj ops per project root.
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/LibGit2.swift:20` — `enum LibGit2`, sole `git_libgit2_init` owner, `static func withRepository<T>(_ root: URL, _ body: (OpaquePointer) -> T?) -> T?` at `:32`. libgit2 1.9.2 is linked DIRECTLY too (`macapp/project.yml:40-42`), so raw C calls like `git_graph_ahead_behind` are available. Existing raw-C users: `Core/GitGraph.swift` (revwalk + `git_graph_reachable_from_any`, `originTips` globbing `refs/remotes/origin/*` at `:102-106`), `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`, `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`.

Resolver pattern — each consumer takes an injected `@Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding` factory defaulting to `VCS.provider(for:)`: `Core/BranchResolver.swift:15` (`resolve(path:vcs:) async -> RootRef`, `timeout: 3`, `withTimeout` + provider self-offload), `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:33`, `Core/DiffResolver.swift:22`, `Core/HistoryModel.swift:8` (`@MainActor ObservableObject`, 0.3s pre-dispatch trailing debounce, cancel-and-replace, `runBlocking { resolve(root).log(...) }` at `:123`).
Models: `Core/VCSModels.swift` — `VCSRef`/`VCSRefKind` (`:116-122`), `VCSPushState` (`:29`), `VCSPushScope` (`:36`), `VCSError` (`:154`) with cases `unsupportedRepo/notFound/lockContention/staleSnapshot/partialData/backendVersion/io`, `VCSRepoKind` (`:165`). `Core/Models.swift:79` `RootRef`, `:70` `RefKind`.
`AppStore.swift:2337` `vcsMetadataDir(path:vcs:)` → `.git` or `.jj`; `:2349` `handleRootBranchChange(projectID:)` refreshes History then re-resolves the label; `:2307` `updateRootBranchWatches()`. `WorkroomFileWatcher` (`Core/WorkroomFileWatcher.swift:24`) FSEvents with leading+trailing coalescing. Workroom status TTLs at `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:14-19` (`localStatusTTL = 15`, `ciStatusTTL = 300`, `ghStatusTTL = 60`).

jj-lib 0.43 side (for reference): `GitFetch`/`push_refs` in jj-lib delegate to a real `git` SUBPROCESS with `GitSubprocessOptions.environment` for `GIT_ASKPASS`, so auth is free there too — but exposing it means new `wr-vcs-core` fns + new `#[uniffi::export]` in `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-uniffi/src/lib.rs` + an xcframework rebuild (`make app-vcs`).

Tests: `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/VCSProviderConformanceTests.swift` (cross-backend parity on a colocated jj+git fixture, helpers `requireTool`/`colocatedFixture`/`sh` at `:459/:476/:616`), `BranchResolverTests.swift` (`private struct StubProvider: VCSProviding` at `:7-23`, closure-injected), `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` (real runner, real repos, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`), `FileTreeTests.swift` (fake runner keyed by executable name), Rust `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/` (real throwaway jj repos, `common/mod.rs` skip policy).

## Constraints / preferences
- STRONGLY prefer shelling out to the `git` / `jj` CLI via `StatusCommandRunning` for anything touching the network (fetch/push/pull) — auth comes free, matches the `gh` precedent, avoids a Rust/UniFFI rebuild. Justify or push back if you disagree.
- Avoid touching the Rust workspace if a CLI shell-out gets the same result — a `make app-vcs` rebuild is expensive.
- Everything must be injectable/testable (the app's whole style is closure-injected seams + stub runners).
- The app is macOS 15+ SwiftUI, Swift 6 strict concurrency (`Sendable`, `@MainActor`).

## What I need from you
1. Decide: extend `VCSProviding` vs a NEW separate protocol (e.g. `VCSRemoteOperating` / a `RemoteResolver` service) for branch-list + remote ops. Argue it. Note that adding non-defaulted members to `VCSProviding` breaks 4+ test stub conformers.
2. Concrete new model types (branch list entry, tracking/divergence counts, last-fetch time, remote state) — full Swift declarations, and say where they go.
3. Exact command lines / API calls per backend for: list branches, current upstream, ahead/behind counts, last-fetch time, fetch, push, pull-with-rebase, switch branch. Cover BOTH git and jj. For jj, be explicit about bookmark-vs-branch semantics and what "switch" and "pull with rebase" even mean there (`jj edit` vs `jj new`; jj auto-rebases descendants).
4. Where last-fetch time comes from concretely (e.g. `.git/FETCH_HEAD` mtime — and what the jj colocated equivalent path is). State the failure mode when it's never been fetched.
5. The service/store layer: a new resolver or model class, its debounce/TTL, how results reach SwiftUI, how it's refreshed (existing FSEvents watchers? a timer for the relative "9 minutes ago" text?), and how in-flight fetch/push state is represented (so the UI can show a spinner and disable the button).
6. Error surfacing: auth failure, no remote, no upstream, `git` not installed, timeout. Map to existing types where possible.
7. Test plan: which existing files to extend, what new files, and what's a unit test vs a real-repo integration test.
8. Sequencing: what's phase 1 (minimum to light up the UI) vs later.

Be concrete and opinionated. Flag any place my assumptions are wrong.

Design the UI layer for a new feature in /Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp. Do not write code files — return a detailed implementation plan with concrete file paths, view/type declarations, and sequencing.

## Feature (user's exact ask)
Add a toolbar to the top of the VCS sidebar (which in this app is the RIGHT INSPECTOR column), positioned ABOVE the "Changes" section header but INSIDE the sidebar. Split into three segments, GitHub-Desktop style (the user supplied a GitHub Desktop screenshot):
1. **Left segment**: a branch icon, then two stacked lines — dim caption "Current Branch" over a bold branch name ("master"), with a trailing ▾ disclosure triangle. Clickable → dropdown listing branches.
2. **Middle segment**: two stacked lines — a bold action title over a dim subtitle. States: bold "Push origin" / dim "Last fetched 9 minutes ago" when there are commits to push; "Pull origin with rebase" when there are commits to pull; and when neither, just the fetch status ("Last fetched X minutes ago"). Also shows a trailing pill badge with a count + ↑ arrow (e.g. "5 ↑"), and a leading ↑ glyph.
3. **Right segment**: a narrow icon-only button (▾ in the screenshot; the user wants a FETCH button as an icon).
Segments are separated by full-height vertical hairline dividers.

## Established facts from exploration (trust these — cite them in your plan)

### Where it goes
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/ChangesPanel.swift:11-262` — `struct RightInspector`: the whole inspector pane. Maps `ActivitySection.subSections` → headers/bodies, hands them to `InspectorSplitView`. `:32` sets `fills: subs.map { $0 == .history }`.
- `ChangesPanel.swift:74-120` `sectionHeader(for:)` builds the "Changes" header (title "Changes", shortcut "⌥⌘C", a refresh button); `:123-137` `sectionBody(for:)` → `ChangesPanel()`, `FilesPanel`, `PullRequestPanel`, `HistoryPanel`.
- `ChangesPanel.swift:229-261` `changesIndicator`/`changesIndicatorLabel` — the `+N`/`-M` + conflict/dot badge in the Changes header.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/InspectorColumn.swift:12-59` — the docked column: `RightInspector()` inside `sidebarCard(topMargin: 0, leadingMargin: 2, vibrant: true)`, width 260–520, leading drag handle.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/RootView.swift:148-173` — `HStack { SidebarColumn / detail / if showInspector { InspectorColumn() } / ActivityBar() }`.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ActivitySection.swift:15-56` — activity rail is `.changes` + `.files`; `subSections` (`:42-47`): `.changes → [.changes, .history, .pullRequest]`, `.files → [.files]`. `:58-64` `InspectorSectionKind.storeIndex` (changes=0, files=1, pullRequest=2, history=3).
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/InspectorPanePolicy.swift:7-14` `InspectorSectionKind`; `:47` `headerHeight = 34`; `:52` `expandedMinHeight = 120`; `:81` `allocate`; `:128` `reallocateOnToggle`.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/InspectorSplitView.swift:40-114` `InspectorPaneViewController` (sticky NSHostingController header of fixed `headerHeight` + body in scroll or fill mode); `:141+` `InspectorSplitContainerController` (NSSplitViewDelegate, weights round-trip to the store); `:466-539` `SectionHeader<Accessory>` (`.accessibilityIdentifier("inspector.header.\(title)")`, `.background(tokens.surface)`, accessory overlaid trailing with `.padding(.trailing, 12)`); `:521-538` `headerLabel` — `HStack(spacing: 7) { chevron 11pt semibold rotate 0→90° width 12; Text(title) .system(size: 11, weight: .semibold); indicator; Spacer }` with `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8)`.

### Existing branch-name display (the "ONE layout for git+jj" header) — reuse its vocabulary
- `ChangesPanel.swift:669-730` `changesHeader`; `:680-696` name in a `.caption` capsule (`.padding(.horizontal, 5).padding(.vertical, 1)`, `.background(.quaternary, in: Capsule())`, `.lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)`, `.help("Bookmark / branch")`), then jj-only change-id `.purple` / commit-id `.blue` in `.system(.callout, design: .monospaced)`, extra ref capsules, description line.

### Reusable chrome
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TitlebarBars.swift:75-84` `TitlebarDivider` — `Rectangle().fill(tokens.border).frame(width: 1, height: 14).padding(.horizontal, 4)`; used in `LeadingTitlebarBar` (`:111`), `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`:157`), `WorkroomSplitView.swift:400,403` — with the rule "only when there's something on both sides".
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:341-440` `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` — an EXISTING 3-group toolbar row (`RunControls | TitlebarDivider | OpenInControl | TitlebarDivider | ✕`), `.frame(height: 28)`, one `.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())` + one `.font(.system(size: PaneToolbarIcon.glyph))` for the whole group. **This is the closest structural precedent.**

`bg`/`fg`; `panel` (bg +5.5% fg — title bar, tab bar, activity bar); `fgMuted` (fg@0.65) / `fgDim` (fg@0.40); `surface` (fg@0.08 — section header background, segmented track, selected row); `border` (fg@0.12 — hairlines, dividers, brackets); `hover` (fg@0.06); `rowHover`/`rowSelection` (OPAQUE); `accent`/`accentSoft`/`accentForeground`; `warning`/`failure`/`conflict`; `diffAddFg`/`diffRemoveFg` (+`…Bg` @0.16). `ThemeService.shared.tokens`, `generation`, posts `.themeDidChange`.

### Non-negotiable conventions
Every control needs `.help(...)` + `.accessibilityLabel(...)` + a stable `.accessibilityIdentifier(...)`. Interactive glyphs need their own `.onHover` (so `.help`'s tracking area installs) AND `.contentShape(Rectangle())`. Active state must be signalled by position/brightness, not hue alone. Formatting: `.swift-format`, 2-space indent, 100 columns; run `make app-format` / `make app-lint`; `make app-generate` (xcodegen) after adding any new `.swift` file.

### Known traps (from hard-won project memory — respect these)
- A SwiftUI window-`toolbar` item's overflow `menuFormRepresentation` caused a 2s AppHang; the window toolbar is kept an EMPTY AppKit `NSToolbar`. So this new "toolbar" must be a plain SwiftUI view INSIDE the inspector, never a `.toolbar` modifier.
- `.textSelection(.enabled)` text swallows real mouseDown so SwiftUI taps don't fire (real-mouse-only bug; synthetic XCUITest clicks pass on buggy code).
- `.onHover` controls are NOT drivable from XCUITest; an accessibility id on an `NSViewRepresentable` wrapper is not queryable.
- `@Default` invalidates SwiftUI ASYNCHRONOUSLY — use `@State` for click-immediate UI.
- Pixel-perfect alignment is expected — fix by construction (uniform insets, centered icons), don't eyeball.
- Joel wants XCUITest coverage for new macapp UI, not just unit tests. See `macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/` — and note `make app-uitest` IGNORES `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so scoped runs need a direct `xcodebuild -only-testing:<Class>/<method>`. There's a `UITestFixture` seam (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/UITestFixture.swift`, `isActive`, `static let vcsProvider` at `:630`, `FixtureVCSProvider` at `:636`) — launch arg `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`.

### Engine reality (a parallel agent is planning this half — assume the data will exist)
Today `VCSProviding` is read-only with NO branch listing, NO fetch/push/pull, NO ahead/behind counts, NO last-fetch time. Assume a new service will provide: a branch/bookmark list, current upstream, ahead/behind counts, a last-fetch `Date?`, and async fetch/push/pull actions with in-flight + error state. Design the UI against a clean injectable view-model/observable and SAY exactly what shape you need from it.

## What I need from you
1. Exact placement decision + how to implement it. Key question: `RightInspector` composes section headers/bodies into an `InspectorSplitView` (an AppKit `NSSplitView` host). Does the toolbar go above the whole split view inside `RightInspector`, or inside `InspectorColumn`? What happens with the `.files` activity section (should the toolbar show there too, or only for `.changes`)? Give a recommendation.
2. Full view decomposition: new file(s) under `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/`, the segment sub-views, the divider approach, exact heights/insets/fonts/tokens so it matches the screenshot AND the app's existing look. Two-line segments in a ~30-40pt bar is tight — give real numbers.
3. The branch dropdown: `Menu` vs a custom popover. Consider that a repo can have hundreds of branches (filter field? grouping local vs remote? a "new branch" affordance?). Note the AppHang trap above and whether `Menu`'s lazy content is safe here. Recommend one.
4. The middle segment's state machine: enumerate every state (no remote / no upstream / never fetched / clean / ahead N / behind N / diverged / fetching / pushing / failed) and the exact title+subtitle+badge for each. Include the relative-time formatting approach and how it stays live ("9 minutes ago" must tick).
5. Store/state wiring: where the observable lives (`AppStore`? a new `@Observable`?), how it keys off the inspector target (`AppStore.inspectorTargetID`/`inspectorTarget`, `AppStore.swift:780-781`), and how it avoids doing work when the inspector is hidden (there's an existing precedent: `focusHistoryIfShown()` gated on `inspectorIsVisible && historySectionShown`).

## 3. Exact commands per backend

Every `git` invocation is prefixed with `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`["-c", "core.fsmonitor="]`) — reuse that constant, don't redeclare it. Every `jj` invocation gets `--color never --no-pager`. Read-only jj gets `--ignore-working-copy`; **mutating jj does NOT** (it must snapshot — see the switch note).

### git — one read covers list + current + ahead/behind

```
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref
    --sort=-committerdate
    --count=<cap+1>
    --format=%(refname)%00%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(worktreepath)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:track)%00%(push:short)%00%(push:track)%00%(symref)
    refs/heads refs/remotes
```
Verified against git 2.55 in your repo. Notes that matter:

- **`%00` NUL field separator, newline record separator.** A refname cannot contain a control char, but `%(worktreepath)` is a filesystem path that can contain a tab — hence NUL, not tab. Parse defensively: skip any record whose field count ≠ 11.
- **`--count=cap+1`** — take one extra to learn `refsTruncated`, the exact idiom `GitProvider.log:25` already uses.
- **Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)`.** That's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose `refname:short` is the bare `origin` — it would put a junk row in the picker. (Also gives you the default branch for free: its symref target → `pickerOrder`'s `defaultBranch`.) This mirrors `GitGraph.originTips:119` skipping the same ref.
- **`%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` is the whole ballgame.** With the default `push.default=simple`, `%(push)` resolves to `<remote>/<same-name>` **even when no upstream is configured** — verified on your `platform` repo: `claude/htp-orphan-rebind` has `upstream=∅` but `push=origin/claude/htp-orphan-rebind`, `push:track=∅` (in sync); `fix/sentry-ernie-8` has `push:track=[gone]`. That *is* the origin/same-name fallback you were about to write a second `rev-list` for. Take `push:*` first, fall back to `upstream:*`, record which in `comparedTo`, and set `pullFrom` only when `upstream:short != push:short`.
- **This is the common Workroom case.** A workroom is `git worktree add -b workroom/<n>` (`internal/vcs/git.go:29`) — no upstream, ever. So `upstream:track` is empty for essentially every workroom, and only `push:track` produces `[gone]` → "not pushed yet". Design around that, not around `@{u}`.
- **Empty `push:track` is ambiguous only if you ignore `push:short`.** `push:short` non-empty + track empty ⇒ genuinely in sync. `push:short` empty ⇒ no remote ⇒ `tracking = nil`.
- `%(worktreepath)` includes the *current* worktree, so nil it out when it equals `workroomPath` (that's why `parseGitRefs` takes it).

**Current ref:** `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)`. Do *not* derive it from `%(HEAD)` — that gives nothing for a detached or unborn HEAD, both of which `GitProvider.currentRef:78-98` already handles correctly. Use `%(HEAD)` only for the per-row `isCurrent` marker.

**Ahead/behind for the toolbar:** the `%(HEAD) == "*"` row's `tracking`. No row current (detached) ⇒ `nil`.

### git — actions

| Action | Command | Dir | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git -c core.fsmonitor= fetch <remote>` | **project root** | 120 |
| push | `git -c core.fsmonitor= push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom | 120 |
| pull | `git -c core.fsmonitor= pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <remoteBranch>` | workroom | 300 |
| switch (local) | `git -c core.fsmonitor= switch <name>` | workroom | 120 |
| switch (remote-only) | `git -c core.fsmonitor= switch --track <remote>/<name>` | workroom | 120 |

- **No `--prune` on fetch.** Omitting it lets the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide — the same "pass NULL and let libgit2 read the repo's config" philosophy documented on `GitCommitDiff`. It also keeps `GitGraph`'s origin tips from silently changing under an unsuspecting user.
- **No `--no-write-fetch-head`.** We *need* `FETCH_HEAD` (§4).
- **`--set-upstream` only when there's no upstream yet** (`tracking?.pullFrom == nil && upstream:short` was empty). Passing it every time rewrites `branch.<n>.remote`/`.merge` on every push.
- **Never `--force`/`--force-with-lease`.** Rejection → `.rejected` → the UI offers Pull. Force-push is not an engine capability in phases 1–3.
- **`--autostash` on pull is mandatory, not optional.** Workroom users always have a dirty tree; without it every pull dies on "cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes".
- **Explicit `<remote> <remoteBranch>` on pull**, derived from `pullFrom ?? comparedTo` minus the `<remote>/` prefix, so a workroom with no configured upstream can still pull. Fall back to bare `git pull --rebase --autostash` only when an upstream exists.
- `git switch` gives you three guards libgit2 does not: the already-checked-out-in-another-worktree refusal, the dirty-tree refusal, and atomic HEAD+index+worktree update. See §9.5.

  ++ "\x00" ++ if(self.remote(), self.remote(), "")

Notes that matter:

- **The keyword is `self`, not `ref`.** `-T 'ref.name()'` errors with "Keyword `ref` doesn't exist".
- **The `tracking_*_count()` guards are not defensive padding.** Calling them on a local (non-remote) ref renders the literal string `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>` into your output. I hit this.
- **Filter out `remote == "git"`.** A colocated repo has a pseudo-remote called `git` (jj's local Git-tracking bookmarks), and `--all-remotes` includes it. Your `platform` repo emits `chore/bundle-update@git` rows. It is not a remote; dropping it also keeps `remotes` clean.
- **jj's counts are stated from the REMOTE ref's perspective and must be swapped.** See §9.2. `parseJJBookmarks` maps `ahead = tracking_behind_count`, `behind = tracking_ahead_count`, and that inversion belongs in one commented line with an integration test pinning it.
- **`present == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `gone = true`.** Verified: `chore/bundle-update@origin` has a blank target and `behind 6010` (its whole local history) — jj's equivalent of git `[gone]`.
- **`tracked == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `comparedTo` set but counts `nil`.** jj cannot answer for an untracked remote bookmark.

- No `--limit` on `bookmark list`; cap in Swift.
- `--ignore-working-copy` is **required** — without it every toolbar read snapshots `@`, taking the working-copy lock (the existing house rule from `VCSProviding:37`, `RustJJProvider:105`).
- Measured 72 ms on a 30-bookmark repo (most of it `jj` startup). Fine behind a 15 s TTL.

**Current ref + kind:** `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)` → `RustJJProvider.currentRef` → the Rust core's `current_ref`, which already does the bookmark-cleaning and nearest-ancestor walk. `kind == .ancestor` ⇒ `hasUnbookmarkedWork = true`.

**Ahead/behind for the toolbar:** the row matching `current.name`. When `kind == .ancestor` those counts describe the *ancestor bookmark*, not your work — which is precisely why `hasUnbookmarkedWork` exists.

### jj — actions (all inside `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`)

| Action | Command | Dir | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <remote> --color never --no-pager` | **project root** | 120 |
| push | `jj git push --remote <remote> --bookmark <name> --color never --no-pager` | **project root** | 120 |
| pull step 1 | `jj git fetch --remote <remote> …` | project root | 120 |
| pull step 2 | `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote> --color never --no-pager` | workroom | 300 total |
| switch | `jj new <name>` (or `<name>@<remote>`) `--color never --no-pager` | workroom | 120 |

- **Gating is not optional.** Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock — I proved it accidentally: `jj git remote list` failed with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"*. A project's workrooms share that lock, which is exactly the class `JJSnapshotGate` was built for. `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` does **not** take it, so reads stay ungated.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "innermost call must be un-timed" rule can be relaxed here, and should be.** That rule exists because `withTimeout` cannot cancel an in-flight jj-lib call, so the gate would release while the abandoned call still physically held the lock. A CLI shell-out is different: `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely dead and the lock genuinely released. Compose as `gate.run(projectRoot:) { await runner.run(…, timeout: n) }` — no outer `withTimeout` needed at all, since the runner's own timeout is real. Document this distinction where you write it; it looks like a violation of the gate's doc and isn't.
- **`jj new`, not `jj edit`.** `jj edit <bookmark>` makes the *bookmarked commit itself* the working copy, so your next keystroke rewrites a commit that is probably already pushed. `jj new <bookmark>` creates a fresh empty `@` on top. `jj new` also leaves `current.kind == .ancestor`, which is exactly what the sidebar already renders (`RootRef.kind == .ancestor` → `"main ↑"`, `Models.swift:146`) — so switching via `jj new` keeps the whole app self-consistent.
- **`jj new` must NOT get `--ignore-working-copy`.** It snapshots first, which is what preserves your uncommitted edits into the old `@` before the working copy is rewritten to the new tree. Suppressing the snapshot risks losing them.
- **jj's switch never refuses on a dirty tree; git's always might.** Don't paper over it — the git path needs a "stash or commit first" error state that the jj path never reaches.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`.** `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@` (your commits that aren't ancestors of the destination) onto the new tip — the pull-rebase shape. `-s @` would move only `@` and its descendants, orphaning its parents.
- **Run the rebase unconditionally.** If `@` is already a descendant, jj prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0. Cheaper than a descendant-check revset, and jj is atomic + `jj undo`-able.
- **Do NOT pass `--skip-emptied`** in phase 1. It would match git's "drop commits that are already upstream", but it also abandons a commit the user deliberately made empty *with a description*. jj's default loses nothing and is undoable. Note the divergence from git in the doc comment; make it a preference later if anyone asks.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts.** Conflicts become part of the commits. Never infer success from the exit code — see §6.

## 4. Last-fetch time: concrete, and **your `FETCH_HEAD` assumption breaks for jj**

**git:** `<worktree gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD` mtime, via `FileManager.attributesOfItem(atPath:)[.modificationDate]`. No subprocess. Resolve the gitdir purely:

- `<path>/.git` is a **directory** (project root) → `<path>/.git/FETCH_HEAD`
- `<path>/.git` is a **file** (workroom worktree) → read it, strip the `gitdir: ` prefix, trim → `<gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD`
- neither → `nil`

Both branches are pure and unit-testable with a temp fixture. (`git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD` is the authoritative equivalent but costs a process for something two `FileManager` calls answer.)

**Because `FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, fetch must run at the project root** — otherwise fetching in workroom A leaves the project root and workroom B reading "never fetched" while their `refs/remotes/*` are perfectly fresh. Running fetch at the project root makes "last fetched" a per-**project** fact that every workroom of that project agrees on, which is also the right UX. This is why `opDirectory` special-cases `.fetch` for git as well as jj.

**jj: `FETCH_HEAD` is never written.** jj-lib 0.43's fetch is a `git` subprocess invoked as
```
git fetch --porcelain --prune --no-write-fetch-head -- <remote> <refspecs>
```
(`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`, with the comment *"--no-write-fetch-head ensures our request is invisible to other parties"*). I confirmed this empirically on your `platform` repo: `jj git fetch` ran at 14:44 and yesterday 20:07 per `jj op log`, while `.git/FETCH_HEAD`'s mtime is 16:57 — written by something else entirely. Reading `FETCH_HEAD` for a jj repo would report a plain `git fetch` you ran in a terminal months ago, or nothing.

So for jj, scan the operation log:

**Fragility, acknowledged:** that description is an English string jj could reword. Mitigations: (a) the failure mode is graceful — one absent label, never a wrong one; (b) match a prefix, not the whole string; (c) an integration test on a real throwaway jj repo pins it, so a jj bump turns the suite red instead of silently blanking the label. **No persisted stamp needed.** After *our own* fetch succeeds, git has written `FETCH_HEAD` and jj has written a fetch op, so a single re-read is authoritative. Zero new persisted state, and a terminal-side `git fetch`/`jj git fetch` shows up too.

**Failure modes to spell out:**
- fresh clone/`init`, never fetched → git `.never` (`clone` does not write `FETCH_HEAD`)
- `fetch.writeFetchHEAD=false` → git `.unknown` forever
- jj repo fetched > 200 ops ago → `.never` (a lie by omission; raise the limit if it bites)
- `.never` and `.unknown` both render **no timestamp**. Never print "never fetched" for `.unknown`.

  @Published private(set) var inFlight: VCSRemoteAction?

  private(set) var target: Target?

  var onDidMutate: (@MainActor (VCSRemoteAction) -> Void)?

       debounce: TimeInterval = 0.3,

  func activate(_ target: Target?)       // the panel's `.task`: refresh on settled re-entry

  func switchTo(_ ref: VCSBranchRef)

**TTL = 15 s**, matching `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:14`'s `localStatusTTL`. Justified: the whole read is *local* — one `for-each-ref` / one `bookmark list`, no network — so it's the same cost class as the local status probe. (`ciStatusTTL = 300` is for network reads; nothing here is one.)

**Refresh triggers — reuse the existing watchers, add none:**

1. **Selection change** → `focus(...)`, debounced 0.3 s (`AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet`).
2. **The existing per-project `.git`/`.jj` FSEvents watcher.** `rootBranchWatchers` (`AppStore:2307-2331`) already watches `vcsMetadataDir(path:vcs:)` **recursively**. That single watcher per project covers everything this feature cares about, for every workroom of that project:
   - git fetch → `<project>/.git/FETCH_HEAD` + `refs/remotes/*` ✓
   - git switch in a workroom → `<project>/.git/worktrees/<n>/HEAD` ✓ (inside the watched tree)

## 6. Error surfacing

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` for success. Ordered checks, matched against strings I verified in the git 2.55 binary on this machine:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| `r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing("git"/"jj")` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| stderr ∋ `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username` \| `could not read Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired(stderr)` |
| stderr ∋ `'…' is already used by worktree at '…'` (also legacy `already checked out`) | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| stderr ∋ `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten` \| `The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree(stderr)` |
| stderr ∋ `There is no tracking information for the current branch.` | `.noUpstream` |
| stderr ∋ `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| `no such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| stderr ∋ `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected(stderr)` |
| stderr ∋ `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists` \| `Unable to create`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge` or `rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other(trimmed stderr, else stdout, else "…exited N")` |

**Deliberately a new enum, not `VCSError`.** `VCSError`'s seven cases are the *backend read* taxonomy and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over them exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge; adding it would force an arbitrary answer in a function that currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution` beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`. **Do** reuse the `CommandResult.commandNotFound`/`gitFatal` sentinels (`StatusCommandRunner:15-17`).

**Surfacing policy:**
- **A failed action never blanks a good snapshot.** `lastFailure` is a separate `@Published`; `snapshot` is untouched. Exactly the `.keepPrior` philosophy already in `applyCIStatus`/`applyPRStatus`.
- Hard failures also raise the store's existing alert (`errorTitle`/`errorMessage`), the `performPRAction:210` pattern: `"Couldn't fetch"` + trimmed stderr, or a hand-written line for the cases where raw stderr is unhelpful:
  - `.authRequired` → "Git couldn't authenticate. Workroom never prompts for credentials — configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH." **This is your #1 failure mode and it needs bespoke copy.** `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally, and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails instantly. That's correct behaviour (never hang), but the raw stderr is baffling.
  - `.toolMissing` → "`git` isn't on Workroom's PATH." Note the app *already* hard-requires both binaries — the Go CLI shells `git worktree add` (`internal/vcs/git.go:29`) and `jj workspace add` (`internal/vcs/jj.go:30`) to create a workroom at all — so this is a real-but-already-fatal condition, not a new dependency. That's also the argument that settles §9.4: no libgit2 fallback needed.
  - `.rebaseInProgress` → "A rebase is in progress in this workroom. Run `git rebase --abort` (or `--continue`) in its terminal." **Do not offer Retry** — it will fail identically.
  - `.nothingToPush` (jj) → "`@` has no bookmark, so there's nothing to push. Set one first."
  - `.alreadyCheckedOut` → "`<branch>` is already checked out in `<path>`."
- **`.timedOut(.pull)` is the dangerous one.** SIGKILLing `git fetch` mid-transfer is safe (git is crash-safe; worst case a stale `objects/pack/tmp_*`). SIGKILLing `git pull --rebase` is **not** — it can leave `rebase-merge/` behind. Hence the generous 300 s budget, and the post-failure `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` probe that upgrades `.timedOut` to `.rebaseInProgress` so the message tells the truth.
- **jj conflicts are not errors.** `jj rebase` exits 0 having written conflicts into commits. So after a jj pull, `classify` returns `nil` and you must ask the working copy: the `onDidMutate` → `refreshWorkroomStatuses(force: true)` already re-reads `WorkroomStatus.conflicted` through `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`. Return `.okWithConflicts` when that comes back conflicted, and lean on jj's `jj undo` in the copy ("Undo in the terminal with `jj undo`") — jj's recovery story here is genuinely better than git's and worth saying out loud.
- `.rejected` → the toast/banner offers **Pull**, never Force.

**Phase 3 — Pull with rebase**

## 9. Where your assumptions need correcting

1. **`jj git fetch` passes `--no-write-fetch-head`**, so `FETCH_HEAD` is *not* the jj last-fetch source. (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`; confirmed empirically on your `platform` repo — op-log fetches at 14:44/20:07 vs a `FETCH_HEAD` mtime of 16:57.) Use the op-log scan (§4).
2. **jj's ahead/behind are inverted.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local* = git's **behind**; `tracking_behind_count()` = git's **ahead**. jj's own default template proves it: `format_tracked_remote_ref_distances` prints `"ahead by N commits"` next to `@origin`. Swap on ingest, comment the swap, pin it with a cross-backend integration test.
3. **`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree.** A fetch in the project root is invisible to a workroom's `FETCH_HEAD` and vice versa. Run fetch at the project root always — which also makes "last fetched" a per-project fact all workrooms agree on. (`ghProbeDirectory`'s rule extends to git, not just jj, for this one op.)
4. **You don't need a second command for ahead/behind, and you don't need `@{u}`.** `git for-each-ref`'s `%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence *even with no upstream configured* — verified on your `platform` repo. That's the fallback chain you were going to hand-roll, plus `[gone]`, plus per-row counts for the picker, plus `%(worktreepath)`, plus `%(HEAD)`, in one 30 ms process.
5. **"SwiftGitX's LOCAL ops are fine" does not extend to `switch`.** `Repository.switch(to:)` → `git_checkout_tree` + `git_repository_set_head`, and **libgit2 does not enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard**. Workroom's entire model is `git worktree add -b`, so a picker offering `main` would happily give you two worktrees on `main` where the CLI refuses. It's also non-atomic (checkout then set-HEAD; a failure between leaves a half-switched repo) and skips the DWIM/hook/submodule behaviour users expect. Shell out.
6. **`Repository.push` silently writes repo config.** Its `addPushRefspec` calls `git_remote_add_push`, persisting `remote.origin.push = refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x` into the repo's config — for every branch you push. Independent of the credentials problem, that alone disqualifies it.
7. **jj workrooms have no bookmark, so git's and jj's Push buttons are not symmetric.** A jj workroom is `jj workspace add --name workroom/<n>` (`internal/vcs/jj.go:30`) — no bookmark is created. So `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` and `jj git push -b <ancestor>` would push the *project's* `master`, not your work. Disable Push with `.nothingToPush` in phase 1; the phase-4 `--named workroom/<n>=@-` is the real fix. A git workroom, by contrast, is a real branch and `push --set-upstream` just works.
8. **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the git import/export lock**, even a read: `jj git remote list` failed with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"* under the sandbox. So don't reach for `jj git remote list`/`jj git root` in the read path — derive the remote list from `jj bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes (free) and locate the git dir by reading `.jj/repo/store/git_target` (verified: contains `../../../.git` on your colocated `platform` repo). `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
9. **`SwiftGitX.Branch.init` is eager and expensive** — one `ObjectFactory.lookupObject`, one `git_branch_upstream` that *recursively constructs another `Branch`* (another object lookup), plus a `git_remote_lookup`, **per branch**. `branch.list(.local)` on a 500-branch repo is ~1500 libgit2 object lookups on a blocking thread. Beyond the runner-injection problem, that's a bad way to fill a menu.
10. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocess ops**, and you should say so where you write it or it'll read as a bug. The rule exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGKILLs the process tree at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone and the lock genuinely released. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Separately: the gate is key-based and backend-agnostic, so if git's `packed-refs.lock` contention shows up in practice, route git remote ops through it too — at which point renaming it (`RepoWriteGate`) costs 3 call sites + `JJSnapshotGateTests.swift`. I'd defer the rename rather than churn it speculatively.
11. **Never auto-fetch.** No TTL-driven, focus-driven, or sweep-driven network call. It burns rate limits, can trigger credential/SSH prompts on a machine nobody's watching, and the existing `refreshWorkroomStatuses` sweep has no business growing a network mutation.

# VCS toolbar: branch selection + push/pull/fetch status

## Context

The VCS inspector today can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only place a branch name appears is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes
body (`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`), both
display-only.

So a user working in a workroom has to leave the app for every remote interaction: they can see what
changed but not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, when they last fetched, or what
other branches exist — let alone act on any of it.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, GitHub-Desktop shaped — current
branch as a dropdown that switches branches, a sync segment that reads "Push origin / Last fetched 9
minutes ago" with an ahead/behind count pill and performs the action on click, and a fetch icon
button. Working for **both** git and jj.

Scope confirmed with the user: **everything** — fetch, push, pull-with-rebase, and branch switch.
Toolbar shows **only when the Changes activity section is active**.

---

## Decisions

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Extend `VCSProviding`? | **No — zero changes.** New `VCSRemoteResolver` struct modelled 1:1 on `WorkroomStatusResolver`. |
| Backend | `git` / `jj` **CLI** via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth comes free (credential helpers, ssh-agent, tokens); matches the existing `gh` precedent. |
| SwiftGitX for network? | **No.** `Repository+fetch.swift:30` / `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct ⇒ zero credential support, HTTPS impossible. `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). |
| SwiftGitX for `switch`? | **No.** libgit2 doesn't enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard — fatal given Workroom *is* worktrees. Also non-atomic, and `Repository.push` silently writes `remote.origin.push` into repo config. |
| Rust / UniFFI | **Zero changes.** No `make app-vcs`. |
| Auto-fetch | **Never.** Explicit user action only. |
| Toolbar visibility | Only when `store.activeInspectorSection == .changes`. |

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift`

Shaped exactly like `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`: one `struct`, an injected
`StatusCommandRunning`, private `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ`, and `static` pure arg-builders/parsers/
classifiers that carry all the semantics (the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern).

```swift
struct VCSRemoteResolver: Sendable {
  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
  /// For `currentRef` only — reuse the app's canonical answer incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`.
  /// Same seam + default as `BranchResolver.swift:20`.
  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5       // local ref listing
  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300    // network + rebase; SIGKILL here is dangerous
  var switchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
  var refCap: Int = 500

  func resolveState(path:vcs:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:vcs:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func switchRef(path:vcs:projectRoot:to:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult

  /// THE placement rule (the `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory:364` pattern).
  static func opDirectory(_ action:path:vcs:projectRoot:) -> String
}
```

Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`, `["-c","core.fsmonitor="]`) verbatim on every
git call. Every jj call gets `--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`,
**mutations must not** (they need to snapshot).

#### git — one process answers list + current + ahead/behind

```
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --count=<cap+1>
  --format=%(refname)%00%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(worktreepath)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:track)%00%(push:short)%00%(push:track)%00%(symref)
  refs/heads refs/remotes
```

- `%00` NUL separators — `%(worktreepath)` is a path and can contain a tab. Skip records whose field
  count ≠ 11 rather than crashing.
- `--count=cap+1` to learn `refsTruncated` (the `GitProvider.log:25` idiom).
- **`%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` is the whole ballgame.** Under the default `push.default=simple`
  they resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence **even with no upstream configured** —
  which is every Workroom branch, since a workroom is `git worktree add -b` (`internal/vcs/git.go:30`).
  Take `push:*` first, fall back to `upstream:*`, record which in `comparedTo`, set `pullFrom` only
  when they differ. No second `rev-list`, no `@{u}`.
- Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name is
  the bare `origin` (junk picker row). Its target gives the default branch for free.
- `%(worktreepath)` includes the *current* worktree, so nil it when it equals the workroom's own path.
  Non-nil ⇒ a `git switch` **will** fail ⇒ the picker disables that row.
- Current ref comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)`, **not** `%(HEAD)` — that returns
  nothing for detached/unborn HEAD, both already handled at `GitProvider.swift:78-98`. `%(HEAD)` is
  only the per-row `isCurrent` marker.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <remoteBranch>` | workroom |
| switch (local) | `git … switch <name>` | workroom |
| switch (remote-only) | `git … switch --track <remote>/<name>` | workroom |

- **No `--prune`, no `--no-write-fetch-head`** — let the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide, and we
  need `FETCH_HEAD`.
- `--set-upstream` **only** when no upstream exists yet; otherwise it rewrites config on every push.
- **Never** `--force` / `--force-with-lease`. Rejection ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ the UI offers Pull.
- `--autostash` on pull is mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.
- Explicit `<remote> <remoteBranch>` on pull (from `pullFrom ?? comparedTo`) so an upstream-less
  workroom can still pull.

#### jj — one process answers list + ahead/behind

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
emitting NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `committer timestamp`, `present`, `conflict`,
`tracked`, `tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`.

Four traps, all verified against jj 0.43 locally:
- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
- `tracking_*_count()` on a non-remote ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`
  into the output — the `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote called `git` that `--all-remotes`
  includes. Not a remote; also keeps `remotes` clean.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means
  *the remote is ahead* = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.

Plus `present == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `gone` (jj's `[gone]`); `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set
but counts `nil`. One record per `(name, remote)`; fold in Swift.

**Anonymous-branch counts.** When `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` (jj `@` carries no bookmark — the
normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark), the bookmark row's
counts describe the *ancestor bookmark*, not the user's work. So when and only when `.ancestor`, run
two extra cheap local revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@'  -T '"x\n"'  → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)'  -T '"x\n"'  → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the ahead count and
the Push button agree by construction.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull step 1 | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | project root |
| pull step 2 | `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` | workroom |
| switch | `jj new <name>` / `jj new <name>@<remote>` | workroom |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): it creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, and names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). This is the answer for the unbookmarked workroom `@` — no
  hand-rolled naming policy, and the user's own template config is honoured.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-`. jj refuses to push a
  commit with an empty description, and a fresh `@` after `jj new` has neither. `WorkroomStatus
  .jjWorkingCopy` (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so the model
  decides this with no extra process.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git
  remote list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"*).
  So all jj mutations go through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`, and the read path derives
  the remote list from `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes instead of calling `jj git remote list`.
  `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned
  call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s
  at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely dead. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }`
  with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this where written — it reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj new`, not `jj edit`.** `jj edit <bookmark>` makes the bookmarked (probably-pushed) commit
  itself the working copy. `jj new` puts a fresh `@` on top and leaves `kind == .ancestor`, which is
  exactly what the sidebar already renders as `"main ↑"` (`Models.swift:146`).
- **`jj new` must not get `--ignore-working-copy`** — it snapshots first, which is what preserves
  uncommitted edits into the old `@`.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run it unconditionally: already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts** — jj records conflicts *inside* commits. Never infer success
  from the exit code; re-read `workingStatus().conflicted` and return `.okWithConflicts`.

#### Last-fetch time — differs per backend

**git:** mtime of `<worktree gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD` via `FileManager.attributesOfItem`. No subprocess.
Resolve the gitdir purely: `.git` as directory ⇒ `<path>/.git/FETCH_HEAD`; `.git` as **file** (the
worktree case) ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, trim.

`FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree**, which is why fetch runs at the project root for git too: fetching
inside workroom A would otherwise leave the project and every sibling workroom reading "never
fetched" while their `refs/remotes/*` are perfectly fresh. Running at the root makes "last fetched" a
per-**project** fact all workrooms agree on.

**jj: `FETCH_HEAD` is never written.** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch --porcelain --prune
--no-write-fetch-head` (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`, *"ensures our request is invisible
to other parties"*). Verified empirically. So scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; take the first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile
against a jj rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure mode (one absent label,
never a wrong one), and an integration test that turns red on a jj bump.

`VCSLastFetch` is a three-way enum (`.at(Date)` / `.never` / `.unknown`), not `Date?` — `.unknown`
must never render as "never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule). No persisted stamp: after our own
fetch, set `.at(Date())` optimistically (the `applyOptimisticPRAction` pattern,
`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:220`) and let the re-read confirm — which also means a `git fetch`
typed in the workroom's own terminal moves the number.

### Error classification — `static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?`

One pure function, `nil` on success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `is already used by worktree at` | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `no tracking information for the current branch` | `.noUpstream` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

`.authRequired` is the **#1 expected failure** and needs bespoke copy: `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets
`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails
instantly (correct — never hang) with baffling stderr. Say: *"Workroom never prompts for credentials
— configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH."*

`.rebaseInProgress` must **not** offer Retry; it needs `git rebase --abort`. `.timedOut(.pull)` gets
upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` by the post-failure probe, because SIGKILLing a rebase mid-flight is
the one genuinely unsafe timeout.

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSSyncPresentation.swift` — pure mapper

`static func make(_ snapshot: VCSSyncSnapshot, now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation`. No SwiftUI, no
`Date()` read — `now` is a parameter so the whole thing is unit-testable at fixed instants (the
`Core/ChangeBadge.swift` precedent). Returns `titleVariants: [String]` (longest first, `[]` ⇒
single-line mode), `subtitle`, `subtitleShort`, `symbol`, `badge`/`secondaryBadge`, `action`,
`isEnabled`, `tone`, `help`, `accessibility`, `accessibilityValue`.

| # | Condition | Title | Subtitle | Badge | Click |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | no target | — | "No workroom selected" | — | — |
| 2 | not a repo | — | "No repository" | — | — |
| 3 | no remote | — | "No remote configured" | — | — |
| 4 | no upstream / `gone` | "Publish branch" | "`<branch>` isn't on origin yet" | `N ↑` | push `--set-upstream` |
| 5 | never fetched, clean | — | "Never fetched" | — | fetch |
| 6 | clean, fetched | — | "Last fetched \(rel)" | — | fetch |
| 7 | ahead only | **"Push origin"** | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `N ↑` | push |
| 8 | behind only | "Pull origin with rebase" | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` | pull |
| 9 | **diverged** | "Pull origin with rebase" | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` then `N ↑` | **pull** |
| 10-12 | fetching/pushing/pulling | "Fetching…"/"Pushing…"/"Pulling…" | "from/to origin" | kept | disabled |
| 13 | failed, idle | previous title | error first line, `tone: .failure` | kept | retry |

Precedence: 13 > 10-12 > 1 > 2 > 3 > 4 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 5 > 6.

Two calls worth pinning with tests:
- **Diverged ⇒ Pull, not Push.** git refuses a non-fast-forward push anyway.
- **No upstream + ahead ⇒ `.publish`, not `.push`.** This is *the* workroom case — a git workroom is
  `git worktree add -b` with no upstream, ever. Getting it wrong makes every workroom read "Push
  origin" against an upstream that doesn't exist.

Relative time: `static func fetchedAgo(_ date:now:short:)` over two `static let
RelativeDateTimeFormatter`s (`.full` / `.abbreviated`); under 60 s ⇒ "just now". Do **not** reuse
`NotificationsList.timeAgo` — it's private and reads `Date()` internally, so it's untestable.

### Layout degradation, 260 → 520pt

At 260 the ideal widths sum to ~287, so it *must* degrade. In firing order:
1. **Sync wins** — `layoutPriority(1)` vs branch `0`. A truncated branch name is still identifiable
   and its full name is repeated in the Changes header 40pt below plus its own tooltip.
2. Truncate, never wrap; every `Text` is `.lineLimit(1)`.
3. Subtitle abbreviates before truncating: "Last fetched 9 minutes ago" → "Fetched 9 min. ago".
4. Title abbreviates: "Pull origin with rebase" → "Pull with rebase" → "Pull".
5. **The "Current Branch" caption drops first** (below ~120pt of branch width) → name only, centred.
   At 260 the caption is not shown. Stated out loud rather than shipping a clipped caption.
6. The sync glyph drops next — the pill's arrow already carries direction.
7. The pill never yields (`.fixedSize()`).
8. Fixed 36pt height at every width; no reflow of the split view below.

Growing to 520: branch caps at 220 so a short name doesn't hoard dead space; sync takes
`maxWidth: .infinity` and absorbs the rest — the extra goes to the segment that can use it.

# VCS toolbar: branch selection + push/pull/fetch status

## Context

The VCS inspector today can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only place a branch name appears is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes
body (`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`), both
display-only.

So a user working in a workroom has to leave the app for every remote interaction: they can see what
changed but not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, when they last fetched, or what
other branches exist — let alone act on any of it.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, GitHub-Desktop shaped — current
branch as a dropdown that switches branches, a sync segment that reads "Push origin / Last fetched 9
minutes ago" with an ahead/behind count pill and performs the action on click, and a fetch icon
button. Working for **both** git and jj.

Scope confirmed with the user: **everything** — fetch, push, pull-with-rebase, and branch switch.
Toolbar shows **only when the Changes activity section is active**.

---

## Decisions

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Extend `VCSProviding`? | **No — zero changes.** New `VCSRemoteResolver` struct modelled 1:1 on `WorkroomStatusResolver`. |
| Backend | `git` / `jj` **CLI** via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth comes free (credential helpers, ssh-agent, tokens); matches the existing `gh` precedent. |
| SwiftGitX for network? | **No.** `Repository+fetch.swift:30` / `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct ⇒ zero credential support, HTTPS impossible. `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). |
| SwiftGitX for `switch`? | **No.** libgit2 doesn't enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard — fatal given Workroom *is* worktrees. Also non-atomic, and `Repository.push` silently writes `remote.origin.push` into repo config. |
| Rust / UniFFI | **Zero changes.** No `make app-vcs`. |
| Auto-fetch | **Never.** Explicit user action only. |
| Toolbar visibility | Only when `store.activeInspectorSection == .changes`. |

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift`

Shaped exactly like `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`: one `struct`, an injected
`StatusCommandRunning`, private `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ`, and `static` pure arg-builders/parsers/
classifiers that carry all the semantics (the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern).

```swift
struct VCSRemoteResolver: Sendable {
  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
  /// For `currentRef` only — reuse the app's canonical answer incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`.
  /// Same seam + default as `BranchResolver.swift:20`.
  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5       // local ref listing
  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300    // network + rebase; SIGKILL here is dangerous
  var switchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
  var refCap: Int = 500

  func resolveState(path:vcs:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:vcs:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func switchRef(path:vcs:projectRoot:to:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult

  /// THE placement rule (the `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory:364` pattern).
  static func opDirectory(_ action:path:vcs:projectRoot:) -> String
}
```

Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`, `["-c","core.fsmonitor="]`) verbatim on every
git call. Every jj call gets `--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`,
**mutations must not** (they need to snapshot).

#### git — one process answers list + current + ahead/behind

```
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --count=<cap+1>
  --format=%(refname)%00%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(worktreepath)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:track)%00%(push:short)%00%(push:track)%00%(symref)
  refs/heads refs/remotes
```

- `%00` NUL separators — `%(worktreepath)` is a path and can contain a tab. Skip records whose field
  count ≠ 11 rather than crashing.
- `--count=cap+1` to learn `refsTruncated` (the `GitProvider.log:25` idiom).
- **`%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` is the whole ballgame.** Under the default `push.default=simple`
  they resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence **even with no upstream configured** —
  which is every Workroom branch, since a workroom is `git worktree add -b` (`internal/vcs/git.go:30`).
  Take `push:*` first, fall back to `upstream:*`, record which in `comparedTo`, set `pullFrom` only
  when they differ. No second `rev-list`, no `@{u}`.
- Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name is
  the bare `origin` (junk picker row). Its target gives the default branch for free.
- `%(worktreepath)` includes the *current* worktree, so nil it when it equals the workroom's own path.
  Non-nil ⇒ a `git switch` **will** fail ⇒ the picker disables that row.
- Current ref comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)`, **not** `%(HEAD)` — that returns
  nothing for detached/unborn HEAD, both already handled at `GitProvider.swift:78-98`. `%(HEAD)` is
  only the per-row `isCurrent` marker.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <remoteBranch>` | workroom |
| switch (local) | `git … switch <name>` | workroom |
| switch (remote-only) | `git … switch --track <remote>/<name>` | workroom |

- **No `--prune`, no `--no-write-fetch-head`** — let the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide, and we
  need `FETCH_HEAD`.
- `--set-upstream` **only** when no upstream exists yet; otherwise it rewrites config on every push.
- **Never** `--force` / `--force-with-lease`. Rejection ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ the UI offers Pull.
- `--autostash` on pull is mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.
- Explicit `<remote> <remoteBranch>` on pull (from `pullFrom ?? comparedTo`) so an upstream-less
  workroom can still pull.

#### jj — one process answers list + ahead/behind

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
emitting NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `committer timestamp`, `present`, `conflict`,
`tracked`, `tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`.

Four traps, all verified against jj 0.43 locally:
- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
- `tracking_*_count()` on a non-remote ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`
  into the output — the `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote called `git` that `--all-remotes`
  includes. Not a remote; also keeps `remotes` clean.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means
  *the remote is ahead* = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.

Plus `present == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `gone` (jj's `[gone]`); `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set
but counts `nil`. One record per `(name, remote)`; fold in Swift.

**Anonymous-branch counts.** When `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` (jj `@` carries no bookmark — the
normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark), the bookmark row's
counts describe the *ancestor bookmark*, not the user's work. So when and only when `.ancestor`, run
two extra cheap local revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@'  -T '"x\n"'  → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)'  -T '"x\n"'  → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the ahead count and
the Push button agree by construction.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull step 1 | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | project root |
| pull step 2 | `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` | workroom |
| switch | `jj new <name>` / `jj new <name>@<remote>` | workroom |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): it creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, and names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). This is the answer for the unbookmarked workroom `@` — no
  hand-rolled naming policy, and the user's own template config is honoured.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-`. jj refuses to push a
  commit with an empty description, and a fresh `@` after `jj new` has neither. `WorkroomStatus
  .jjWorkingCopy` (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so the model
  decides this with no extra process.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git
  remote list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"*).
  So all jj mutations go through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`, and the read path derives
  the remote list from `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes instead of calling `jj git remote list`.
  `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned
  call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s
  at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely dead. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }`
  with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this where written — it reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj new`, not `jj edit`.** `jj edit <bookmark>` makes the bookmarked (probably-pushed) commit
  itself the working copy. `jj new` puts a fresh `@` on top and leaves `kind == .ancestor`, which is
  exactly what the sidebar already renders as `"main ↑"` (`Models.swift:146`).
- **`jj new` must not get `--ignore-working-copy`** — it snapshots first, which is what preserves
  uncommitted edits into the old `@`.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run it unconditionally: already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts** — jj records conflicts *inside* commits. Never infer success
  from the exit code; re-read `workingStatus().conflicted` and return `.okWithConflicts`.

#### Last-fetch time — differs per backend

**git:** mtime of `<worktree gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD` via `FileManager.attributesOfItem`. No subprocess.
Resolve the gitdir purely: `.git` as directory ⇒ `<path>/.git/FETCH_HEAD`; `.git` as **file** (the
worktree case) ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, trim.

`FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree**, which is why fetch runs at the project root for git too: fetching
inside workroom A would otherwise leave the project and every sibling workroom reading "never
fetched" while their `refs/remotes/*` are perfectly fresh. Running at the root makes "last fetched" a
per-**project** fact all workrooms agree on.

**jj: `FETCH_HEAD` is never written.** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch --porcelain --prune
--no-write-fetch-head` (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`, *"ensures our request is invisible
to other parties"*). Verified empirically. So scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; take the first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile
against a jj rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure mode (one absent label,
never a wrong one), and an integration test that turns red on a jj bump.

`VCSLastFetch` is a three-way enum (`.at(Date)` / `.never` / `.unknown`), not `Date?` — `.unknown`
must never render as "never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule). No persisted stamp: after our own
fetch, set `.at(Date())` optimistically (the `applyOptimisticPRAction` pattern,
`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:220`) and let the re-read confirm — which also means a `git fetch`
typed in the workroom's own terminal moves the number.

### New models — appended to `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSModels.swift`

`VCSTracking { comparedTo, ahead: Int?, behind: Int?, gone, pullFrom }` — counts always from the
*local* ref's view; `nil` means unanswerable, never zero.
`VCSBranchRef { name, scope: .local/.remote(String), commitID, committedAt, isCurrent, checkedOutIn, tracking }`.
`VCSLastFetch { at(Date), never, unknown }`.
`VCSRemoteState { current: VCSRef, tracking, hasUnbookmarkedWork, refs, remotes, primaryRemote, lastFetch, resolvedAt, refsTruncated }`.

At the top of `VCSRemoteResolver.swift` (the `CIResolution`/`PRResolution` placement precedent):
`VCSRemoteAction { fetch, push, pull, switchRef }`,
`VCSRemoteFailure { toolMissing, timedOut, authRequired, noRemote, noUpstream, rejected, dirtyWorkingTree, alreadyCheckedOut, rebaseInProgress, locked, other }`,
`VCSRemoteResolution { state, absent, keepPrior, failed }`,
`VCSRemoteActionResult { ok, okWithConflicts, failed }`.

**Deliberately not folded into `VCSError`** — that enum is the *backend read* taxonomy and
`WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over it exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge.
`.authRequired` has no sidebar badge; adding it would force a meaningless answer there.

### Error classification — `static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?`

One pure function, `nil` on success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `is already used by worktree at` | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `no tracking information for the current branch` | `.noUpstream` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

`.authRequired` is the **#1 expected failure** and needs bespoke copy: `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets
`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails
instantly (correct — never hang) with baffling stderr. Say: *"Workroom never prompts for credentials
— configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH."*

`.rebaseInProgress` must **not** offer Retry; it needs `git rebase --abort`. `.timedOut(.pull)` gets
upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` by the post-failure probe, because SIGKILLing a rebase mid-flight is
the one genuinely unsafe timeout.

`@MainActor final class RemoteStateModel: ObservableObject`, owned by `AppStore` as a third sibling

`var onDidMutate: (@MainActor (VCSRemoteAction) -> Void)?` wired by the store post-init (the
`lazy var workroomFileWatcher` idiom) so the model unit-tests with no `AppStore`.

**ObservableObject, not `@Observable`** — the whole tree is `@EnvironmentObject`, and `HistoryModel`/
`FileTreeModel` are `ObservableObject`. Mixing observation systems buys nothing.
