### Error classification

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` on
success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `Host key verification failed` | `.hostKeyUnverified` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<common gitdir>/worktrees/<n>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

Copy that matters:
- `.authRequired` — *"Workroom never prompts for credentials. Load your key into ssh-agent, or
  configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`)."* With D5 this
  fails instantly instead of hanging; with D17 agent users don't reach it at all.
- `.hostKeyUnverified` — *"`<host>` isn't in your known_hosts. Connect once from a terminal to accept
  its key."* `BatchMode=yes` makes this a hard failure rather than a stall.
- `.rebaseInProgress` — *"A rebase is in progress in this workroom."* Offers **Abort rebase**, never
  Retry (D14).
- `.rejected` — offers **Pull**, never Force.

input.plan:
# VCS toolbar: branch label + push/pull/fetch status

> Revised after `/plan-eng-review`. 7 review findings + 25 outside-voice findings folded across 17
> decisions (D3–D19). **Branch switching was cut (D14)**; two verified engine bugs were fixed
> (D13, D15). See the review report at the end.

## Context

The VCS inspector can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only branch name on screen is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes body
(`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and one in the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`).

So a user in a workroom leaves the app for every remote interaction: they can see what changed but
not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, or when they last fetched.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, shown only when the Changes
activity section is active. Current branch as a read-only label, a sync segment that reads
"Push origin / Last fetched 9 minutes ago" with an ahead/behind pill and performs the action on
click, and a fetch icon. Working for both git and jj.

**Cut during review (D14):** branch *switching*. Workrooms **are** branches — identity is the
directory basename (`internal/vcs/git.go:70-80`; no `branch` key in `internal/config/`) — so
switching a workroom's branch makes its name permanently wrong, and the jj path was reproduced
deleting a working-copy file and orphaning the workroom's commit. Segment 1's click opens the
existing ⌘O workroom picker instead. "New workroom from branch…" is filed as the product-correct
successor.

---

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D3 | Write ops go behind a **new** `VCSWriting` protocol + `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by a CLI-backed type holding the injected runner. `VCSProviding` untouched — reads stay structurally unable to mutate. Supersedes `TODOS.md:118`. |
| D4 | **git** write ops also route through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`. Worktrees share one `.git`; a lock loss mid-`pull --rebase` wedges a workroom. Rename deferred. |
| D5 | `StatusCommandRunner` pins `stdin` to `/dev/null` and, for network ops, sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` + `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, clearing `SSH_ASKPASS`/`DISPLAY`. |
| D6 | Two ASCII diagrams, in this plan and mirrored as code comments. |
| D7 | The post-pull conflict determination lives in the **model**, after the gate releases — not in the writer. |
| D8 | One state struct. The mapper takes `(state, activity, failure, pullRebase, now)`. `VCSSyncSnapshot` deleted. |
| D9 | All four branch-name implementations unify onto **one shared cache**. |
| D10 | A counting stub asserts a branch-label read spawns **zero** VCS calls. |
| D11 | The UI-test fixture records requested actions; 4 flow tests assert the button→engine seam. |
| D12 | Remote-ref data is cached **per project root**, not per workroom. |
| D13 | Ahead/behind come from `git rev-list --left-right --count`. **`%(push:*)` is deleted** — see below. |
| D14 | **Switch cut.** Push + pull stay; pull gains a `rebase --abort` affordance. |
| D15 | A workroom reads the **shared** git dir's `FETCH_HEAD`, not its own. |
| D16 | **Auto-fetch on inspector focus**, interval-guarded. Knowingly supersedes `TODOS.md:324`. |
| D17 | Forward `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`/`SSH_AGENT_PID`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` from `ShellEnvironment.environment()` for network ops only. |

**Backend:** shell out to `git`/`jj` via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth is the user's own agent and
credential helpers; the app already shells `gh`. SwiftGitX is unusable for this — `Repository+fetch.swift:30`
and `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct, so there is no credential path at all, and
`pull` doesn't exist. **Zero Rust/UniFFI changes; no `make app-vcs`.**

### Two bugs the review caught, both verified on git 2.55

**`%(push:track)` does not work for the branches this product creates.** Under `push.default=simple`
— git's built-in default — a branch with no upstream yields `PUSH=[]` and `PUSHT=[]`. Only `current`
and `matching` populate them. Every workroom is `git worktree add -b` (no upstream), so the headline
count would be blank on any machine not set to `current`. It looked fine only because this machine is
`current`. Measured:

```
push.default=simple    UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
push.default=current   UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[origin/feat]     PUSHT=[[gone]]
push.default=upstream  UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (what the integration test does)  PUSH=[] PUSHT=[]
```

**`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so fetching at the root never writes the workroom's copy.**
`git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD` returns `.git/FETCH_HEAD` at the root but
`.git/worktrees/<n>/FETCH_HEAD` inside a workroom. The original plan fetched at the root *and* read
the per-worktree path — so every workroom would have read "never fetched" forever.

---

## Diagrams

### Operation routing (D6 — mirror above the writer's `opDirectory`)

```
                 ┌──────────────── every network op ────────────────┐
                 │ stdin=/dev/null · BatchMode=yes · askpass=never   │  D5
                 │ + SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_CONFIG_*    │  D17
                 └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                        │
              ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
              │   JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)         │  D4 (git too)
              │   never re-enter for the same root  ── D7         │
              └─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                                        │
        git ────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────── jj
                                        │
  fetch   → PROJECT ROOT                │        fetch  → PROJECT ROOT
           (FETCH_HEAD is per-worktree; │                 (workspace has no .git)
            root = one shared answer)   │        push   → PROJECT ROOT
  push    → workroom                    │                 (bookmarks are repo-global)
  pull    → workroom (fetch step: root) │        pull    → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
                                        │
  READ (ungated, no lock):              │        READ (ungated, --ignore-working-copy):
   for-each-ref refs/remotes  ──┐       │         bookmark list --all-remotes  ──┐
   rev-list --left-right --count ┤ D13  │         (+ 2 revset counts if @        ┤
   stat <common-gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD ┘ D15│          is unbookmarked)              ┘
                                        │         op log → last fetch
```

### Sync-segment state precedence (D6 — mirror above `VCSSyncPresentation.make`)

Three orthogonal axes collapse to one order. Read top-down; first match wins.

```
  failure?  ──yes──►  [13] retry previous action        tone: failure
     │no
  in flight? ──yes──►  [10/11/12] Fetching…/Pushing…/Pulling…    disabled
     │no
  target valid? ──no──►  [1] no workroom  ·  [2] no repository    disabled
     │yes
  has remote? ──no───►  [3] "No remote configured"               disabled
     │yes
  upstream missing / gone? ──yes──►  [4] "Publish branch"   → push --set-upstream
     │no
  ahead>0 && behind>0 ──yes──►  [9] "Pull <remote> with rebase"  badge: M↓ then N↑
     │no                              (pull, NOT push — git refuses non-ff)
  behind>0 ──yes──►  [8] "Pull <remote> with rebase"             badge: M↓
     │no
  ahead>0  ──yes──►  [7] "Push <remote>"                         badge: N↑
     │no
  never fetched ──yes──►  [5] "Never fetched"          → fetch
     │no
                        [6] "Last fetched <rel>"       → fetch
```

`<remote>` is interpolated from `primaryRemote`, **never** the literal "origin" —
`remote.pushDefault` can make that wrong (verified: `-c remote.pushDefault=upstream` →
`PUSH=[upstream/feat]`).

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift`

A new protocol + one CLI-backed conformer + `VCS.writer(for:)`, alongside the existing
`VCS.provider(for:)` (`VCSProviding.swift:87`). This is the growth surface for the rest of Phase 2
(commit/amend, bookmark management, jj split/absorb/undo), which is why it's a protocol and not a
standalone resolver — but it is deliberately **separate** from `VCSProviding` so a read path cannot
reach a mutation.

```swift
protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func abortRebase(path:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult          // D14
}

enum VCS {
  /// Routes by `repoKind(at:)`, same as `provider(for:)`. Throws `.unsupportedRepo`.
  static func writer(for root: URL, projectRoot: URL,
                     runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
                     makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
                       = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) }) throws -> VCSWriting
}
```

One conformer, `CLIVCSWriter`, holds the runner (the reason this can't go on `VCSProviding` —
`GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere
to put it). It switches on repo kind internally and keeps all semantics in `static` pure
arg-builders/parsers/classifiers — the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern.

Timeouts: `refTimeout 5`, `fetch/push 120`, `pull 300`, gate `.shared`.
Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`) verbatim on every git call. jj gets
`--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`, **mutations must not**.

`currentRef` comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)` — the app's existing canonical answer
including `.ancestor`/`.detached`. Do not re-derive it.

### git — reads

```
# 1. remote refs + the remotes list (no cap needed — the picker is gone)
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --format='%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(symref)' refs/remotes

# 2. exact two-way divergence, config-independent  (D13)
git -c core.fsmonitor= rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>
```

- **Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)`** — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name
  is the bare remote. Its target also yields the default branch for free.
- `primaryRemote` = `origin` if present, else the first remote, else `nil`.
- The counterpart ref is `refs/remotes/<primaryRemote>/<current-branch>`, existence-checked against
  the list from (1). Absent ⇒ state 4 ("Publish branch"), no counts — this is the workroom default.
- `rev-list` runs only when the counterpart exists. Output is `<ahead>\t<behind>`.
- **`%(push:*)` and `%(upstream:*)` are not used for counts.** That also dissolves the "upstream is a
  local branch" case (measured: `UP=[main] UPT=[[ahead 3]] PUSH=[]`), because we only ever compare
  against `refs/remotes/`.

**Last fetch (D15):** mtime of `<common gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD`. Resolve purely — `.git` as a directory
⇒ `<path>/.git`; `.git` as a **file** ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, then strip the trailing
`/worktrees/<name>` to reach the common dir. No subprocess. Unit-test all three shapes plus a
malformed pointer.

### git — actions

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … fetch <remote>` (root), then `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| abort | `git … rebase --abort` | workroom |

No `--prune` (let `fetch.prune` decide), no `--no-write-fetch-head` (we need it), **never**
`--force`/`--force-with-lease`. `--set-upstream` only when there is no upstream yet. `--autostash` is
mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.

### jj — reads

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `present`, `conflict`, `tracked`,
`tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`. Verified on jj 0.43:

- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref`.
- The `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing — calling
  `tracking_*_count()` on a local ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has that pseudo-remote and `--all-remotes` includes it.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means the
  *remote* is ahead = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.
- `present == 0` ⇒ `gone`. `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set, counts `nil`.
- Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated. Measured ~72ms on a 30-bookmark repo.

**Anonymous `@`** (`currentRef.kind == .ancestor` — the normal workroom state, since
`jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark): the bookmark row's counts describe the *ancestor*, not
the user's work. Only then, two extra revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@' -T '"x\n"'   → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)' -T '"x\n"'   → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the count and the
button agree by construction.

**Last fetch:** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch … --no-write-fetch-head`
(`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`), so `FETCH_HEAD` is never written — confirmed
empirically. Scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile to a jj
rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure (one absent label, never a wrong one),
and an integration test that reddens on a jj bump.

### jj — actions (all inside the gate)

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` (root), then `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` (workroom) | — |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). No hand-rolled naming policy.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-` — jj refuses to push a commit
  with an empty description, and a fresh `@` has neither. `WorkroomStatus.jjWorkingCopy`
  (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so this costs no process. Pure
  decision function; unit-test it.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git remote
  list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export"*). So derive the remote list from
  `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes; never call `jj git remote list` on the read path.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, but `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout`
  and `killTree`s at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone. Compose
  `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this — it
  reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run unconditionally; already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts.** Never infer success from the exit code — see D7.

### Error classification

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` on
success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `Host key verification failed` | `.hostKeyUnverified` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<common gitdir>/worktrees/<n>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

Copy that matters:
- `.authRequired` — *"Workroom never prompts for credentials. Load your key into ssh-agent, or
  configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`)."* With D5 this
  fails instantly instead of hanging; with D17 agent users don't reach it at all.
- `.hostKeyUnverified` — *"`<host>` isn't in your known_hosts. Connect once from a terminal to accept
  its key."* `BatchMode=yes` makes this a hard failure rather than a stall.
- `.rebaseInProgress` — *"A rebase is in progress in this workroom."* Offers **Abort rebase**, never
  Retry (D14).
- `.rejected` — offers **Pull**, never Force.

### New: `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift`

`@MainActor final class RemoteStateModel: ObservableObject`, owned by `AppStore` as a third sibling to
`fileTree` (`AppStore.swift:400`) and `commitHistory` (`:407`). Cloned structurally from
`Core/HistoryModel.swift`: same `State`/`isSettled`, the **0.3s pre-dispatch trailing debounce**,
cancel-and-replace, `focus`/`activate`/`refresh(force:)`/`awaitCurrentLoad()`, and the injection seam.
`ObservableObject`, not `@Observable` — the whole tree is `@EnvironmentObject`.

(separate from `state`, so a failed action never blanks a good snapshot — the `.keepPrior` rule).

**Per-project cache (D12):** `remotes` + `primaryRemote` + the counterpart-exists answer are keyed by
**project root** with a 15s TTL, shared by every workroom of that project. Only `current`, `tracking`
and `lastFetch` are per-workroom. Matches how `rootRefs` is already keyed.

**D7 — conflict determination:** the writer returns `.ok`. `onDidMutate` → `refreshWorkroomStatuses(force: true)`
lands, and the **model** upgrades the outcome to conflicted from `WorkroomStatus.conflicted`. The
writer must never read working status inside the gate — `JJSnapshotGate.swift:66-70` documents that
re-entering for the same root deadlocks that project's queue for `maxChainWait` (30s) and then
self-heals by running *unserialized*.

**D16 — auto-fetch:** on inspector focus, gated on `inspectorIsVisible && activeInspectorSection == .changes`,
with a per-project interval guard (default 5 min) and a hard skip under `UITestFixture.isActive`. An
auto-fetch failure is **silent** — it sets `lastFailure` for the tooltip but raises no alert and never
blocks the read path. This knowingly supersedes `TODOS.md:324`.

questions.question:
D22 — What minimum versions should Workroom declare? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-version-floor>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`. Relevant facts: jj-lib 0.43 pins `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION = "2.41.0"` for its own git subprocess (`git_subprocess.rs:48`); the app's Rust core is built against jj-lib 0.43; the plan's git usage needs nothing newer than about 2.9.

ELI10: A floor is a promise: below this, we refuse rather than fail weirdly. Pick it too low and you're claiming to work on versions nobody tested. Pick it too high and you lock out users for no reason. The principled anchor is that jj already refuses to work with git older than 2.41 in colocated repos, so anything below that is already unsupported for half your users — and pinning jj to 0.43 matches the jj-lib the app links, which matters because an older CLI may not understand the repo format that library writes.

Recommendation: A — git 2.41 and jj 0.43, both anchored to something real rather than picked. Not arbitrary, easy to justify in the warning text, and it covers every command the plan issues with room to spare.

Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.

options.label: git 2.41 / jj 0.43 (recommended)
options.description:
Anchor both to something already true rather than chosen.

✅ git 2.41 is jj's own declared minimum, so it's a floor your jj users already live under — nothing new is excluded.
✅ jj 0.43 matches the jj-lib the app links, which avoids an older CLI meeting a repo format the linked library wrote.
✅ Comfortably above everything the plan issues (`%(symref)` needs 2.8, `pull --autostash` needs 2.9).

options.label: git 2.30 / jj 0.30 — permissive
options.description:
Lower floors covering older distro and enterprise baselines.

✅ Excludes almost nobody — git 2.30 shipped in 2021 and is a common long-term-support baseline.
✅ Still above every flag the plan actually uses.
❌ Claims support for versions nothing is tested against, and jj below ~0.18 doesn't even have `jj bookmark` (it was `jj branch`), so the jj floor would be a promise the code cannot keep.

options.label: git 2.55 / jj 0.43 — what's verified
options.description:
Declare exactly the versions every finding in this review was verified against.

✅ Total honesty: the floor is precisely what has been tested, with no inference about older behaviour.
✅ Simplest possible support story.
❌ git 2.55 is very recent, so this would warn on a large share of otherwise-fine installs — turning a safety net into noise for users whose git works perfectly.

questions.question:
D23 — How should the below-floor warning behave? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-version-warning>

ELI10: You asked for a warning at app start. The open question is what it does beyond appearing. Plan updated. Changes since your feedback:

**D24 added** — `git >= 2.41` **required**, `jj >= 0.43` **optional but floor-checked when present**. Probed in the background at app start, after `ShellEnvironment` sets the PATH floor (the probe needs PATH to find the binaries).

Floors are anchored, not picked: 2.41 is the minimum **jj itself** enforces for its git subprocess (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:48`), so it excludes nobody a jj user isn't already excluded by; 0.43 matches the jj-lib the Rust core links, which matters because an older CLI may not understand the repo format that library writes.

Your required/optional distinction made the check **per project VCS** rather than global:

| Condition | git project | jj project | Warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| git ok, jj absent | enabled | actions disabled | **only** if a jj project is registered |
| git ok, jj below floor | enabled | actions disabled | jj-specific |
| git below floor | disabled | disabled | git-specific — a colocated jj repo drives git underneath |
| git absent | disabled | disabled | broken install |

So an old `jj` never disables a git project's toolbar, and a git-only machine with no `jj` gets no warning and doesn't even spawn `jj --version`. `.unknown` from a timed-out probe counts as ok — never cry wolf.

This closes the review's one critical failure gap, so **critical gaps: 0**. The version floor moved out of the TODO list (T17 now files 3 entries, not 4) and became **T18 (P1)**, sequenced at build step 3 alongside the runner hardening — it gates every action added later, so it has to exist first.

# VCS toolbar: branch label + push/pull/fetch status

> Revised after `/plan-eng-review`. 7 review findings + 25 outside-voice findings folded across 17
> decisions (D3–D19). **Branch switching was cut (D14)**; two verified engine bugs were fixed
> (D13, D15). See the review report at the end.

## Context

The VCS inspector can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only branch name on screen is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes body
(`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and one in the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`).

So a user in a workroom leaves the app for every remote interaction: they can see what changed but
not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, or when they last fetched.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, shown only when the Changes
activity section is active. Current branch as a read-only label, a sync segment that reads
"Push origin / Last fetched 9 minutes ago" with an ahead/behind pill and performs the action on
click, and a fetch icon. Working for both git and jj.

**Cut during review (D14):** branch *switching*. Workrooms **are** branches — identity is the
directory basename (`internal/vcs/git.go:70-80`; no `branch` key in `internal/config/`) — so
switching a workroom's branch makes its name permanently wrong, and the jj path was reproduced
deleting a working-copy file and orphaning the workroom's commit. Segment 1's click opens the
existing ⌘O workroom picker instead. "New workroom from branch…" is filed as the product-correct
successor.

---

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D3 | Write ops go behind a **new** `VCSWriting` protocol + `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by a CLI-backed type holding the injected runner. `VCSProviding` untouched — reads stay structurally unable to mutate. Supersedes `TODOS.md:118`. |
| D4 | **git** write ops also route through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`. Worktrees share one `.git`; a lock loss mid-`pull --rebase` wedges a workroom. Rename deferred. |
| D5 | `StatusCommandRunner` pins `stdin` to `/dev/null` and, for network ops, sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` + `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, clearing `SSH_ASKPASS`/`DISPLAY`. |
| D6 | Two ASCII diagrams, in this plan and mirrored as code comments. |
| D7 | The post-pull conflict determination lives in the **model**, after the gate releases — not in the writer. |
| D8 | One state struct. The mapper takes `(state, activity, failure, pullRebase, now)`. `VCSSyncSnapshot` deleted. |
| D9 | All four branch-name implementations unify onto **one shared cache**. |
| D10 | A counting stub asserts a branch-label read spawns **zero** VCS calls. |
| D11 | The UI-test fixture records requested actions; 4 flow tests assert the button→engine seam. |
| D12 | Remote-ref data is cached **per project root**, not per workroom. |
| D13 | Ahead/behind come from `git rev-list --left-right --count`. **`%(push:*)` is deleted** — see below. |
| D14 | **Switch cut.** Push + pull stay; pull gains a `rebase --abort` affordance. |
| D15 | A workroom reads the **shared** git dir's `FETCH_HEAD`, not its own. |
| D16 | **Auto-fetch on inspector focus**, interval-guarded. Knowingly supersedes `TODOS.md:324`. |
| D17 | Forward `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`/`SSH_AGENT_PID`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` from `ShellEnvironment.environment()` for network ops only. |
| D24 | **`git >= 2.41` is required; `jj >= 0.43` is optional but floor-checked when present.** Probed at app start; below floor ⇒ a persistent notification **and** remote actions disabled, scoped per project VCS. In scope, not a TODO. |

**Backend:** shell out to `git`/`jj` via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth is the user's own agent and
credential helpers; the app already shells `gh`. SwiftGitX is unusable for this — `Repository+fetch.swift:30`
and `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct, so there is no credential path at all, and
`pull` doesn't exist. **Zero Rust/UniFFI changes; no `make app-vcs`.**

### Two bugs the review caught, both verified on git 2.55

**`%(push:track)` does not work for the branches this product creates.** Under `push.default=simple`
— git's built-in default — a branch with no upstream yields `PUSH=[]` and `PUSHT=[]`. Only `current`
and `matching` populate them. Every workroom is `git worktree add -b` (no upstream), so the headline
count would be blank on any machine not set to `current`. It looked fine only because this machine is
`current`. Measured:

```
push.default=simple    UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
push.default=current   UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[origin/feat]     PUSHT=[[gone]]
push.default=upstream  UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (what the integration test does)  PUSH=[] PUSHT=[]
```

**`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so fetching at the root never writes the workroom's copy.**
`git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD` returns `.git/FETCH_HEAD` at the root but
`.git/worktrees/<n>/FETCH_HEAD` inside a workroom. The original plan fetched at the root *and* read
the per-worktree path — so every workroom would have read "never fetched" forever.

---

## Diagrams

### Operation routing (D6 — mirror above the writer's `opDirectory`)

```
                 ┌──────────────── every network op ────────────────┐
                 │ stdin=/dev/null · BatchMode=yes · askpass=never   │  D5
                 │ + SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_CONFIG_*    │  D17
                 └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                        │
              ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
              │   JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)         │  D4 (git too)
              │   never re-enter for the same root  ── D7         │
              └─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                                        │
        git ────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────── jj
                                        │
  fetch   → PROJECT ROOT                │        fetch  → PROJECT ROOT
           (FETCH_HEAD is per-worktree; │                 (workspace has no .git)
            root = one shared answer)   │        push   → PROJECT ROOT
  push    → workroom                    │                 (bookmarks are repo-global)
  pull    → workroom (fetch step: root) │        pull    → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
                                        │
  READ (ungated, no lock):              │        READ (ungated, --ignore-working-copy):
   for-each-ref refs/remotes  ──┐       │         bookmark list --all-remotes  ──┐
   rev-list --left-right --count ┤ D13  │         (+ 2 revset counts if @        ┤
   stat <common-gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD ┘ D15│          is unbookmarked)              ┘
                                        │         op log → last fetch
```

### Sync-segment state precedence (D6 — mirror above `VCSSyncPresentation.make`)

Three orthogonal axes collapse to one order. Read top-down; first match wins.

```
  failure?  ──yes──►  [13] retry previous action        tone: failure
     │no
  in flight? ──yes──►  [10/11/12] Fetching…/Pushing…/Pulling…    disabled
     │no
  target valid? ──no──►  [1] no workroom  ·  [2] no repository    disabled
     │yes
  has remote? ──no───►  [3] "No remote configured"               disabled
     │yes
  upstream missing / gone? ──yes──►  [4] "Publish branch"   → push --set-upstream
     │no
  ahead>0 && behind>0 ──yes──►  [9] "Pull <remote> with rebase"  badge: M↓ then N↑
     │no                              (pull, NOT push — git refuses non-ff)
  behind>0 ──yes──►  [8] "Pull <remote> with rebase"             badge: M↓
     │no
  ahead>0  ──yes──►  [7] "Push <remote>"                         badge: N↑
     │no
  never fetched ──yes──►  [5] "Never fetched"          → fetch
     │no
                        [6] "Last fetched <rel>"       → fetch
```

`<remote>` is interpolated from `primaryRemote`, **never** the literal "origin" —
`remote.pushDefault` can make that wrong (verified: `-c remote.pushDefault=upstream` →
`PUSH=[upstream/feat]`).

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift`

A new protocol + one CLI-backed conformer + `VCS.writer(for:)`, alongside the existing
`VCS.provider(for:)` (`VCSProviding.swift:87`). This is the growth surface for the rest of Phase 2
(commit/amend, bookmark management, jj split/absorb/undo), which is why it's a protocol and not a
standalone resolver — but it is deliberately **separate** from `VCSProviding` so a read path cannot
reach a mutation.

```swift
protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func abortRebase(path:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult          // D14
}

enum VCS {
  /// Routes by `repoKind(at:)`, same as `provider(for:)`. Throws `.unsupportedRepo`.
  static func writer(for root: URL, projectRoot: URL,
                     runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
                     makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
                       = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) }) throws -> VCSWriting
}
```

One conformer, `CLIVCSWriter`, holds the runner (the reason this can't go on `VCSProviding` —
`GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere
to put it). It switches on repo kind internally and keeps all semantics in `static` pure
arg-builders/parsers/classifiers — the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern.

Timeouts: `refTimeout 5`, `fetch/push 120`, `pull 300`, gate `.shared`.
Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`) verbatim on every git call. jj gets
`--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`, **mutations must not**.

`currentRef` comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)` — the app's existing canonical answer
including `.ancestor`/`.detached`. Do not re-derive it.

### git — reads

```
# 1. remote refs + the remotes list (no cap needed — the picker is gone)
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --format='%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(symref)' refs/remotes

# 2. exact two-way divergence, config-independent  (D13)
git -c core.fsmonitor= rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>
```

- **Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)`** — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name
  is the bare remote. Its target also yields the default branch for free.
- `primaryRemote` = `origin` if present, else the first remote, else `nil`.
- The counterpart ref is `refs/remotes/<primaryRemote>/<current-branch>`, existence-checked against
  the list from (1). Absent ⇒ state 4 ("Publish branch"), no counts — this is the workroom default.
- `rev-list` runs only when the counterpart exists. Output is `<ahead>\t<behind>`.
- **`%(push:*)` and `%(upstream:*)` are not used for counts.** That also dissolves the "upstream is a
  local branch" case (measured: `UP=[main] UPT=[[ahead 3]] PUSH=[]`), because we only ever compare
  against `refs/remotes/`.

**Last fetch (D15):** mtime of `<common gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD`. Resolve purely — `.git` as a directory
⇒ `<path>/.git`; `.git` as a **file** ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, then strip the trailing
`/worktrees/<name>` to reach the common dir. No subprocess. Unit-test all three shapes plus a
malformed pointer.

### git — actions

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … fetch <remote>` (root), then `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| abort | `git … rebase --abort` | workroom |

No `--prune` (let `fetch.prune` decide), no `--no-write-fetch-head` (we need it), **never**
`--force`/`--force-with-lease`. `--set-upstream` only when there is no upstream yet. `--autostash` is
mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.

### jj — reads

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `present`, `conflict`, `tracked`,
`tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`. Verified on jj 0.43:

- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref`.
- The `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing — calling
  `tracking_*_count()` on a local ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has that pseudo-remote and `--all-remotes` includes it.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means the
  *remote* is ahead = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.
- `present == 0` ⇒ `gone`. `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set, counts `nil`.
- Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated. Measured ~72ms on a 30-bookmark repo.

**Anonymous `@`** (`currentRef.kind == .ancestor` — the normal workroom state, since
`jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark): the bookmark row's counts describe the *ancestor*, not
the user's work. Only then, two extra revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@' -T '"x\n"'   → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)' -T '"x\n"'   → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the count and the
button agree by construction.

**Last fetch:** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch … --no-write-fetch-head`
(`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`), so `FETCH_HEAD` is never written — confirmed
empirically. Scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile to a jj
rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure (one absent label, never a wrong one),
and an integration test that reddens on a jj bump.

### jj — actions (all inside the gate)

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` (root), then `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` (workroom) | — |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). No hand-rolled naming policy.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-` — jj refuses to push a commit
  with an empty description, and a fresh `@` has neither. `WorkroomStatus.jjWorkingCopy`
  (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so this costs no process. Pure
  decision function; unit-test it.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git remote
  list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export"*). So derive the remote list from
  `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes; never call `jj git remote list` on the read path.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, but `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout`
  and `killTree`s at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone. Compose
  `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this — it
  reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run unconditionally; already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts.** Never infer success from the exit code — see D7.

### Models — appended to `Core/VCSModels.swift`

`VCSTracking { comparedTo, ahead: Int?, behind: Int?, gone }` — counts from the *local* ref's view;
`nil` means unanswerable, never zero.
`VCSLastFetch { at(Date), never, unknown }` — three-way, not `Date?`; `.unknown` must never render as
"never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule).
`VCSRemoteState { current: VCSRef, tracking: VCSTracking?, remotes: [String], primaryRemote: String?, lastFetch: VCSLastFetch, resolvedAt: Date }`

**Cut by review:** `VCSBranchRef` and its `checkedOutIn`/`committedAt`/`isCurrent` (no picker — D14);
`refCap`/`refsTruncated`/`pickerOrder` (nothing enumerates 500 refs any more); `VCSTracking.pullFrom`,
`hasUnbookmarkedWork` (redundant with `current.kind == .ancestor`), per-row tracking, and
`VCSRemoteFailure.noUpstream`/`.alreadyCheckedOut` (D3, D14).

At the top of `VCSWriting.swift`: `VCSRemoteAction { fetch, push, pull, abortRebase }`,
`VCSRemoteFailure { toolMissing, timedOut, authRequired, hostKeyUnverified, noRemote, rejected, dirtyWorkingTree, rebaseInProgress, locked, other }`,
`VCSRemoteResolution { state, absent, keepPrior, failed }`,
`VCSRemoteActionResult { ok, failed }` — deliberately **not** folded into `VCSError`, which is the
backend-*read* taxonomy that `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over
exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge.

### Error classification

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` on
success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `Host key verification failed` | `.hostKeyUnverified` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<common gitdir>/worktrees/<n>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

Copy that matters:
- `.authRequired` — *"Workroom never prompts for credentials. Load your key into ssh-agent, or
  configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`)."* With D5 this

### New: `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` (D24)

Old tools were the review's one critical failure gap: `git for-each-ref` fails **atomically** on an
unknown atom (verified — `--format='%(bogusatom)'` produces `fatal: unknown field name`, no partial
output), and `jj bookmark` was `jj branch` before ~0.18 with `tracking_*_count()` newer still. The app
bundles neither binary — `ShellEnvironment.path()` takes whatever is on PATH. So one old tool turned
the whole feature into `.other` with raw stderr. Declaring a floor closes it.

**git is required; jj is optional.** Both are floor-checked when present, but they mean different
things: no `git` is a broken install (the Go CLI shells `git worktree add` to create a workroom at
all), whereas no `jj` is the normal state for a git-only user and must be silent.

```swift
enum VCSToolVersions {
  static let gitFloor = SemVer(2, 41, 0)   // jj-lib 0.43's own MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION
  static let jjFloor  = SemVer(0, 43, 0)   // the jj-lib the app links

  enum Status: Equatable, Sendable { case ok(SemVer), belowFloor(SemVer), notInstalled, unknown }
  struct Report: Equatable, Sendable {
    let git: Status            // required
    let jj: Status             // optional — `.notInstalled` is not a problem on its own
    /// Whether remote actions are permitted for a project of this VCS. git projects need only git;
    /// jj projects need both, since a colocated jj repo drives git underneath.
    func allowsRemoteActions(vcs: String) -> Bool
    /// Warnings to publish. Never includes jj `.notInstalled` unless a jj project is registered.
    func warnings(hasJJProject: Bool) -> [ToolWarning]
  }

  static func parseGit(_ stdout: String) -> SemVer?   // "git version 2.55.0" / Apple's "(Apple Git-154)"
  static func parseJJ(_ stdout: String) -> SemVer?    // "jj 0.43.0"
  static func probe(runner: StatusCommandRunning, probeJJ: Bool) async -> Report
}
```

**Why these numbers, not arbitrary ones:** git 2.41 is the floor **jj itself** enforces for its git
subprocess (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:48` `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION = "2.41.0"`), so it excludes
nobody a jj user isn't already excluded by; and jj 0.43 matches the jj-lib the Rust core links, which
matters because an older CLI may not understand the repo format that library writes. Both sit
comfortably above what the plan actually issues (`%(symref)` needs 2.8, `pull --autostash` needs 2.9).

**Scoping is per project VCS, not global.** A git project's toolbar must not be disabled because the
user's `jj` is old, and vice versa. Concretely:

| Condition | git project | jj project | Warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| git ok, jj ok | enabled | enabled | none |
| git ok, jj absent | enabled | actions disabled | only if a jj project is registered |
| git ok, jj below floor | enabled | actions disabled | yes, jj-specific |
| git below floor | actions disabled | actions disabled | yes, git-specific (jj drives git underneath) |
| git absent | actions disabled | actions disabled | yes — broken install; workroom creation is already impossible |

**When:** background, at app start, *after* `ShellEnvironment` sets the PATH floor
(`WorkroomApp.swift:23`) — the probe needs PATH to find the binaries at all. One `git --version` and,
only when a jj project is registered, one `jj --version`; 5s each, never blocking launch.

**Below floor ⇒ two consequences, kept in agreement:**
1. A persistent notification via the existing `NotificationCenterStore` (the left-sidebar list, issue
   #118) naming both the found and required versions. Non-modal — a too-old tool must never stop the
   app being useful for terminals and diffs, which issue none of these commands.
2. `canFetch`/`canPush`/`canPull` AND in `allowsRemoteActions(vcs:)`, so the actions disable with the
   reason in their `.help(...)`. The warning and the behaviour agree; nobody sees a warning *and* then
   the raw-stderr failure it was meant to prevent.

`.notInstalled` (exit 127) stays a **distinct** state from `.belowFloor` — different copy, and for git
it is effectively fatal. `.unknown` (probe timed out or output unparseable) is treated as **ok** —
never cry wolf, the same rule `classifyGitHubCLI` (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:425-444`) follows.

| Step | Modules touched | Depends on |

| A. Runner hardening (T5, T6) | `Core/` (StatusCommandRunner, ShellEnvironment) | — |

**Lane A → B → D → E → F** is the spine. **Lane C runs in parallel with A+B** — it touches
`AppStore` and three view files that nothing else in the spine needs until E.

touch `AppStore.swift` and `Views/`. Different files, but if run in separate worktrees, land C before
E and expect an `AppStore.swift` merge. Everything after E is sequential.

Execution: **launch A and C in parallel worktrees. Merge both. Then B → D → E → F sequentially.**

content.text:
I've completed the first three build steps. Let me pause here and report, since this is a natural checkpoint before the largest piece.

**Done and verified — 1413 unit tests pass, 0 failures, build/format/lint clean:**

**1. Remote-state models** (`Core/VCSModels.swift`) — `VCSTracking`, `VCSLastFetch`, `VCSRemoteState`. The doc comments record why counts come from `rev-list` rather than `%(push:track)`, and that jj's counts arrive inverted, so the next person doesn't rediscover either.

**2. Runner hardening** (`Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`, +8 tests) — `stdin` pinned to `/dev/null`, and a new `runNetwork` with `BatchMode=yes`, `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, `SSH_ASKPASS`/`DISPLAY` cleared, and the five auth vars forwarded from the shell probe. Added as a protocol requirement with a forwarding default, so none of the existing test doubles broke.

Two things I changed from the plan while implementing:
- The BatchMode test is **differential** (compares `run` vs `runNetwork`) rather than asserting a literal empty value — an absolute assertion would fail on a machine that legitimately exports `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`.
- A user's own `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` is **appended to**, not replaced — it commonly carries `-i <key>`, which a replace would silently break.

**3. Version floor** (`Core/VCSToolVersions.swift`, +26 tests) — git ≥ 2.41 required, jj ≥ 0.43 optional, with your required/optional split enforced per project VCS. Reused the app's existing `SemanticVersion` rather than writing a second version comparator.

Three deviations worth flagging:
- **`NotificationCenterStore` was the wrong home.** Reading it, every entry is keyed `(targetID, tabID)` and its only `Kind` is `.osc` — a click routes back to a live terminal, which a machine-wide tool problem doesn't have. Using it meant fabricating IDs and teaching click-routing about entries with no terminal. Instead the warning is a standing toast in the existing `ToastStack`, which already hosts two distinct toast kinds, so it followed a pattern rather than fighting one. It doesn't auto-dismiss, because the condition doesn't.
- The probe is **single-flighted process-wide** (`VCSToolVersionCache`), since `AppStore` is per-window and would otherwise spawn `git --version` per window. It remembers whether it probed jj, so a probe taken before any jj project existed doesn't later report a phantom "jj isn't installed".
- Probing is **skipped under XCTest** as well as fixture mode — `apply()` runs in dozens of unit tests and each would otherwise spawn a real process. Same guard `WorkroomApp.init` already uses for the shell probe.

**Next** is task 4, the `VCSWriting` layer — the largest piece, and where the two verified P1 bugs get fixed. Want me to keep going, or would you rather review these three first?

content.text:
Confirmed asymmetry — and it breaks the plan for jj:

- **git**: `FETCH_HEAD` mtime updates on **every** fetch, no-ops included. Plan works.
- **jj**: a fetch with nothing to bring prints `Nothing changed.` and creates **no op-log entry**. So the op log means "last fetch that *changed* something" — a user clicking Fetch with nothing new would see a stale timestamp.

Fixing with a hybrid: the writer reports the backend's own evidence, and the model takes `max(that, our own recorded fetch)`. Checking the Defaults convention.

| Step | What landed |
|---|---|
| 1 | Remote-state models — `VCSTracking`, `VCSLastFetch`, `VCSRemoteState` |
| 2 | Runner hardening — stdin pinned, ssh `BatchMode`, auth vars forwarded (+8 tests) |
| 3 | Version floor — git ≥ 2.41 required / jj ≥ 0.43 optional, per-VCS scoped (+26 tests) |
| 4 | `VCSWriting` protocol + `CLIVCSWriter` — both P1 bug fixes (+54 tests) |
| 5 | `VCSSyncPresenter` — 13-state machine (+29 tests) |

**Three things I verified against real tools rather than trusting the plan:**

1. **The jj templates work** — including that `main@git` (the colocated pseudo-remote) really does appear in `--all-remotes` output and must be dropped.
2. **`jj git fetch` doesn't write `FETCH_HEAD`** — confirmed absent, so the op-log scan is genuinely necessary.
3. **The git read path end-to-end on this repo** — `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` is present as a symref (confirming the drop is needed), and `rev-list --left-right --count` returns `5\t0`, matching your screenshot exactly and identically under `push.default=simple`.

**One new bug found and fixed, which the plan had wrong:**

A `jj git fetch` that brings nothing prints `Nothing changed.` and records **no operation at all**. So the op-log scan means "last fetch that *changed* something" — a user clicking Fetch with nothing new would watch a stale timestamp sit there. git doesn't have this problem (it rewrites `FETCH_HEAD` on every fetch, verified). Fixed with a `vcs.lastFetch` Defaults key: the writer reports the backend's own evidence, and the model will take `max(that, our own recorded fetch)`, so a terminal-side fetch still wins when it's newer.

**Two of my own tests I caught being bad and rewrote:**
- A BatchMode assertion that would flake on any machine exporting `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` → made differential.
- The "no VCS calls" guard was **vacuous** — I built a counter, never wired it to anything, and asserted zero. Replaced with a cost assertion: 2000 reads must finish in under 0.5s, which a single subprocess would blow past. Runs in 0.013s.

**Remaining:** `RemoteStateModel` + store wiring (7), the toolbar itself with fetch live (8), push and pull (9), UI + `file://` integration tests (10), `TODOS.md` (11), final gate (12).

**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. **Fetch, push
and pull-with-rebase have SHIPPED** (the VCS toolbar). What remains: commit/amend, bookmark (jj) /
branch (git) management, and the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog, interdiff).

**Where the write seam actually is — this changed.** The original plan put write methods on
`VCSProviding` with a `CLIVCSProvider` fallback. That is **not** what shipped, and new work should not
follow it. Writes live behind a **separate** `VCSWriting` protocol (`Core/VCSWriting.swift`) with its
own factory `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by `CLIVCSWriter`. Two reasons, both load-bearing:

- `VCSProviding`'s doc calls it "the single seam the app **reads** VCS data through", and four
  resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no gate. A `fetch` on that protocol means
  nothing structurally stops a read path firing a network mutation — the opposite of what
  `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee.
- A CLI-backed method needs an injected `StatusCommandRunning`, and `GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are
  stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one. A new conformer has
  somewhere.

So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.

**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up. The authoritative scope + sequencing live
in the issue #59 plan; this entry is the pointer that makes it discoverable.

**How to start:** Read `Core/VCSWriting.swift` — its doc comment carries the routing diagram, the
per-backend command table and the placement rules (fetch always runs at the project root, for both
backends; jj push too, because bookmarks are repo-global). The read layer blocks nothing. What's left
of the error taxonomy is one-sided (git still flattens to `.io`), and the stale-working-copy **repair**
is itself a write, so it belongs to this phase.

**Depends on:** the VCS read foundation (shipped, Phase 1) and the write seam (shipped with the
toolbar). Spans `Core/VCSWriting.swift`, possibly `vcs/` (Rust) + `WrVcs` UniFFI for native jj ops, and
new write-flow UI.

**Priority:** P2 (the product direction; large — see the plan for the real breakdown).

### Gate git VCS *reads*, not just writes (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up

**What:** Route git status reads through the same per-project `JJSnapshotGate` the writes now use.

**Why:** The toolbar's write path gates git as well as jj, because a project's workrooms are
`git worktree add` worktrees sharing ONE `.git` — a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a workroom
wedged in a rebase. But that only half-closes the contention: `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit`
never touches the gate (only `resolveJJ` does), so a fetch writing `packed-refs` while the ungated
status sweep runs `git status` across N sibling worktrees reproduces exactly the
`packed-refs.lock could not be obtained` failure the gate's own doc cites.

**Pros:** removes the last window where `.locked` is an *expected* outcome rather than an anomaly, so
the UI's Retry affordance becomes a genuine edge case.

**Cons:** serialising reads could measurably slow the status sweep, which fans out per workroom by
design. This wants measurement first — it may be that read/write contention is rare enough in practice
that the cost isn't worth it.

**Context / how to start:** `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit` (the ungated read) vs `resolveJJ` (the
gated one); `CLIVCSWriter.gated` for how the writes do it. Note the gate is key-based and
backend-agnostic, so if this lands, renaming `JJSnapshotGate` → `RepoWriteGate` (3 call sites + its
test suite) stops being speculative churn and starts being accurate.

**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (a real but narrow race; needs measurement before it's worth the sweep's latency).

### jj sibling-workspace staleness after a rebase (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up

**What:** Detect and surface when a jj operation in one workroom leaves a *sibling* workspace stale.

**Why:** All workrooms of a jj project share one repo and op-store. `jj rebase -b @` — what
pull-with-rebase runs — rewrites commits, and any other workspace whose `@` descends from a rewritten
commit is marked stale and needs `jj workspace update-stale` before its next command. Today that
surfaces as an unexplained error in a **different** workroom from the one the user acted in, which is
the worst attribution problem available: nothing on screen connects cause to effect.

**Pros:** turns a mystery error into an explained one, and the repair is a single command Workroom
could offer as a button.

**Cons:** needs a cheap way to detect staleness across workspaces without reading each one (a per-op
check would multiply the cost of every pull).

**Context / how to start:** `VCSStatusFailure.staleWorkingCopy` already exists in the taxonomy, and
`RustJJProvider.workingStatus` already maps jj's stale-working-copy error onto it — so the detection
half may largely exist; the gap is noticing it for a workroom the user is NOT looking at, and offering
the repair. The repair is itself a write, so it belongs on `VCSWriting`.

**Depends on:** pull-with-rebase (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (jj projects only; wrong-workroom errors are rare but very confusing).

### "New workroom from branch…" (macapp) — the successor to branch switching

**What:** Pick a local or remote branch and create a workroom for it, from the VCS toolbar's branch
segment or the ⌘O picker.

**Why:** Branch *switching* was deliberately cut from the VCS toolbar. A workroom's identity IS its
branch — `internal/vcs/git.go` creates it with `git worktree add -b`, and there is no `branch` field
anywhere in `internal/config` — so switching a workroom's branch makes its directory name permanently
wrong, with nothing to reconcile the two. The jj equivalent is worse: `jj new <bookmark>` on the
bookmark the toolbar already displays was reproduced **removing a file from the working copy** and
leaving the workroom's commit as a nameless dangling head, with no visible change in the UI.

But the underlying need — "I want to work on that other branch" — is real, and creating a workroom is
the answer the product model actually supports. The toolbar's branch segment currently routes to ⌘O,
which only lists workrooms that already exist.

**Pros:** gives the cut affordance a correct home; makes an existing remote branch a first-class
starting point instead of requiring a manual create-then-checkout.

**Cons:** needs a branch list (the toolbar deliberately stopped enumerating refs when the picker was
cut), and a naming policy for the new workroom.

**Context / how to start:** `Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift` is the searchable, project-grouped picker
to clone; the Go CLI's `create` already accepts a branch. `CLIVCSWriter.gitRemoteRefsArgs` shows how to
enumerate remote refs cheaply, and its doc explains why the symref row must be dropped.

**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (a real gap, but ⌘O plus a terminal covers it today).

All twelve steps done. **1580 tests pass, 0 failures**; build, format and lint clean. Nothing committed — the change is staged in your working tree for review.

## What shipped

5 new source files, 8 modified, 9 new test files. 14 untracked files, ~1075 lines changed in the tracked ones.

| Layer | File |
|---|---|
| Engine | `VCSWriting.swift` — protocol, `VCS.writer(for:)`, `CLIVCSWriter` |
| | `VCSToolVersions.swift` — git ≥ 2.41 required, jj ≥ 0.43 optional |
| | `VCSSyncPresentation.swift` — the 13-state mapper |
| Model | `RemoteStateModel.swift` |
| View | `VCSToolbar.swift` |

## Bugs found and fixed that the plan had wrong

1. **`%(push:track)` is empty for every workroom.** Under git's default `push.default=simple`, a branch with no upstream — which is what `git worktree add -b` creates — yields nothing. The count would have been blank on any machine not set to `current`, and mine is. Replaced with `rev-list --left-right --count`; the integration suite asserts identical counts under all five `push.default` values.

2. **`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree.** Fetching at the project root never writes the workroom's copy, so "last fetched" would have read *never* forever. Now resolves the common git dir.

3. **A jj fetch that brings nothing records no operation at all.** The op-log scan alone means "last fetch that *changed* something" — clicking Fetch with nothing new would leave a stale timestamp. Added a `vcs.lastFetch` stamp; the backend still wins when newer, so terminal-side fetches stay visible.

4. **`layoutPriority` inverted the toolbar's sizing** — only caught by running it. `feature/login` rendered as `fe…gin` in a 410pt inspector.

5. **`perform` required a remote for every action**, including abort — which would have left a wedged rebase unrecoverable from the UI.

6. **`awaitCurrentLoad` awaited in the wrong order**, and **`--allow-new` doesn't exist on jj 0.43** (a silently-failing fixture push).

## Two things I want to flag

**The UI tests are written and compile, but I could not run them.** XCUITest fails with *"Timed out while enabling automation mode"* — the recorded automation wedge, triggered by my repeated app launches during the visual check. It needs a login-session reset, which I wasn't going to do to your machine. So the 14 UI tests in `VCSToolbarUITests` are **unverified**. Everything else is: 1580 unit tests, plus 16 integration tests against real git and jj repos over `file://` remotes.

**I wrote two bad tests and caught them.** A BatchMode assertion that would flake on any machine exporting `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, and — worse — a "no VCS calls" guard that built a counter, never wired it to anything, and asserted zero. That one could never fail. Both replaced with assertions that can.

Also worth knowing: `@CommandsBuilder` caps at 10 children and the app was already at 10, so the Source Control menu needed a `Group` wrapper. And I extracted `isAppShortcut` into a pure classifier so the shortcut reservations finally have tests — that list has shipped broken twice.

The automation subsystem had recovered on its own, so the retry worked. Three failures were real, and one of them was serious.

**The bug the UI tests caught — this would have shipped.** `VCSToolbar` observed `AppStore`, but `RemoteStateModel` is its own `ObservableObject` and nothing forwards its `objectWillChange`. So the toolbar rendered the first state and then never repainted: clicking Push set `inFlight`, ran the push, recorded the failure — and the UI showed **none of it**. It would have looked like a dead button.

`HistoryPanel` and `FilesPanel` take their model as an explicit `@ObservedObject` for precisely this reason; I'd read those files and still missed it. No unit test could have found it — it only exists in the wiring between a live view and a live model.

**A second real bug:** the persisted `vcs.lastFetch` stamp leaked across launches, so an earlier test's fetch overrode a seeded `.never` and "Never fetched" read as "just now". Fixed by resetting it in `applyFixtureDefaults`, alongside the inspector-layout pin that exists for the same class of reason.

**Two were my test's fault:** the fixture's 0.6s action delay was shorter than XCUITest's ~1s predicate polling, so the in-flight window fell between samples (raised to 2.5s, with the reasoning written down); and I was clicking a wrapper element rather than the `Button` — SwiftUI publishes the identifier on several layers, and the wrapper reports both `exists` and `isHittable` while swallowing the click. Added a `button(_:id:)` helper that matches `app.buttons` specifically.

That last one is worth remembering: `isHittable` returning true is **not** evidence that a click will invoke the action.

content.text:
Fixed, verified, 3/3 pass.

**Cause:** compounding dim. Text sat at `fgMuted` (fg @ 0.65), then `.opacity(0.4)` multiplied on top — effective **0.26**, fainter than `fgDim` (0.40), which is the *placeholder* tier. I'd copied the `0.4` from `ToolbarIconButtonStyle:58`, where it's correct because it sits on full-strength `fg` (1.0 × 0.4 = 0.40).

**Two different fixes, because the two segments mean different things:**

- **Sync segment** — dropped the blanket dim entirely. Every disabled state there is a *message*, not a withheld action: "No remote configured", "No repository", "Pushing…", and the `.failure`-toned retry line. All must be readable, and the blanket was dimming error copy too. Suppressed hover already says "not clickable".
- **Fetch segment** — kept the dim but as one tier, not a multiply: glyph renders at `fgDim` when disabled. It *is* a bare affordance, so unavailable should read as unavailable.

Hierarchy now: `feature/login` strongest, "No remote configured" at `fgMuted` above it, "Current Branch" caption at `fgDim`, fetch glyph at `fgDim`. The message outranks its label, which is the right way round — before, it sank below it.

Worth noting no test could catch this: opacity isn't in the accessibility tree, and `.disabled` was never wrong. Only looking at it finds it — same class as the `@ObservedObject` miss. That's the second styling/wiring defect this feature has produced that only a real render surfaced, which strengthens the case for the manual QA pass before landing (real remote push/pull, failure copy, the 260→520 resize ladder, real-mouse hover).

All six changes done and verified together in the last screenshot.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit | **1582 passed, 0 failed**, 1 skipped |
| UI — git + jj toolbar suites | **30 passed, 0 failed** (15 × 2 backends) |
| Build / format / lint | clean |

**What changed**

1. **"No remote configured" too faint** — double dim: `fgMuted` (fg @ 0.65) × `.opacity(0.4)` = 0.26, *below* `fgDim`'s 0.40 placeholder tier. I'd copied the 0.4 from `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`, where it's correct because it sits on full-strength `fg`. Dropped it on the sync segment entirely — every disabled state there is a **message** ("No repository", "Pushing…", and the `.failure`-toned retry line), and the blanket was dimming error copy too. Kept it on the fetch segment as one tier (`fgDim`), since that one really is a bare affordance.

2. **Branch segment is display-only** — no `Button`, no hover well, no chevron. Tooltip and right-click "Copy Bookmark Name" remain; neither is a click action.

3. **Branch name out of the Changes panel.** For git that leaves no header at all, so the divider went too. For jj the header keeps `@`'s change-id/commit-id/refs/description — and I had to delete the `extraRefs` filter: it existed to suppress whichever ref the pill was already showing, so with the pill gone it would have **hidden** the bookmark instead.

4. **File-count badge** in the Changes header (`7`, matching the 7 rows). Deliberately outside the line-counts branch — an untracked-only dirty tree has files but no computable `+/−`, so the count is the only thing there is to say.

5. **"Last" dropped** — "Fetched 9 minutes ago"; "ago" already places it in the past.

6. **Equal-width segments** — one shared `segmentMinWidth = 114` replacing the 100/126 split and the 220 cap. Equal width needs the same floor *and* the same `maxWidth`: an `HStack` splits slack evenly, so different minimums stay different by their gap at every width.

**Two things worth flagging**

The jj caption wasn't just the wrong word — it was **absent**. `ViewThatFits` measures each variant's *ideal* width, and a `.lineLimit(1)` truncating `Text` reports its full untruncated string, so the caption was vetoed by a long **name**, never by a narrow cell. jj names ran longer, so jj lost it and git kept it — exactly the asymmetry you saw. The ladder is gone; the caption is unconditional.

Second: **`.accessibilityValue` silently stopped working** when the segment stopped being a `Button`. It read back as `""` and failed two tests. Both parts now live in the label (`"Current Bookmark: feature/login"`), which is the field that reliably carries what's set.

**On the fixture and parity.** The fixture had always fed jj-*shaped* status while declaring `vcs: "git"` — which is precisely why a jj-only wording bug could ship unseen. Added `-WorkroomUITestJJProject 1` and split the suite into `VCSToolbarGitUITests` / `VCSToolbarJJUITests` over a shared base, so all 15 tests run for both. I made it opt-in rather than flipping the default because ~17 other tests depend on that project's shape.

One real caveat: the **jj suite requires `jj` ≥ 0.43 on PATH**, since a jj project's remote actions are gated on both tool floors. It passes here (0.43.0) and it's documented in the file, but on a machine without jj those state tests will fail — correctly, but they will fail.

Nothing is committed; all of this is in your working tree.
Commit. Next todo?

All three verified now. Two of the three changed on contact.

**1. Stale `index.lock` — real, and worse than the review framed it**

Verified: a leftover lock gives `fatal: Unable to create '…/index.lock': File exists.` My `classify` maps `.lock` + `File exists` → `.locked`, whose copy is *"The repository was busy. Try again."* with a **Retry** button.

That's the defect: for a *stale* lock, Retry can never succeed. It's the one failure in the taxonomy whose offered remedy is guaranteed to fail, and the user gets no hint that the fix is deleting a file.

How a stale lock happens: the runner SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and SIGKILLs at `+timeout+2`. git handles SIGTERM and cleans up, so only a git that ignores SIGTERM for two seconds — wedged on a dead network mount, say — reaches SIGKILL and leaves the lock. Narrow window, but SIGKILL is uncatchable so the lock is certain when it happens. (Reasoned, not tested — timing that reliably is fiddly.)

The hooks half is milder than stated: `pull --rebase` fires `post-rewrite`/`post-checkout`, and those inherit the app's env — the deterministic floor plus shell probe, not a full interactive shell — so a hook depending on `nvm`/`rbenv` shims can behave differently than in a terminal. A *prompting* hook is already handled: stdin is `/dev/null`, so it EOFs instead of hanging.

**Open question:** detect a stale lock and offer "Remove stale lock" instead of Retry?

**2. jj `push-<id>` — half real, half disproven**

Accumulation confirmed. Two changes pushed → two bookmarks on the remote, permanent, never cleaned up:
```
push-rrxukuporqwy
push-slxllnxlmxwz
```

But the "non-fast-forward asymmetry" is **a non-issue**. Amending and re-pushing the same change:
```
bookmark: push-slxllnxlmxwz [move sideways from b7e44fc98f79 to 8f82f551ad69]
```
No force flag, no error, no new bookmark — the change id is stable across amends, so jj moves its own bookmark sideways. The review bundled a real problem with an imagined one; correcting what I told you earlier.

Worth noting the accumulation isn't Workroom's invention — it's exactly what bare `jj git push --change` does. We're inheriting jj's behaviour, not choosing a naming policy.

**Open question:** leave it (matches jj), offer cleanup, or require a bookmark before pushing?

**3. `DiffModeSwitch` / `MarkdownModeSwitch` — real but trivial**

Their `segment` builders are identical apart from the active comparison and where the symbol comes from: same 9.5pt font, same 6/3 padding, same corner radii, same `.isSelected` trait. About 40 duplicated lines in one file. Pre-existing, nothing to do with this branch.

**My take on filing:** file #1 (the Retry dead end is a genuine bug). File #2 narrowed to accumulation only, recording that the fast-forward half is disproven so nobody re-investigates it. **Don't** file #3 — a `SegmentedIconSwitch<Value: Equatable>` generic is a single sitting's work, and a TODO entry costs more to maintain than the fix. Either do it or leave it.

**Why:** A jj workroom is `jj workspace add`, whose `@` carries no bookmark, so the toolbar's Push runs
`jj git push --change @`. jj creates a bookmark named by `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
`"push-" ++ change_id.short()`), and **nothing ever removes it**. Verified on jj 0.43 against a bare
origin — two pushes of two different changes left two bookmarks behind permanently:

```
push-rrxukuporqwy
push-slxllnxlmxwz
```

On a shared remote that accrues indefinitely, one entry per change anyone ever pushed from a workroom.

**Not a problem, though it was filed as one:** the review paired this with a suspected
non-fast-forward asymmetry — that re-pushing an amended change would be rejected. It isn't. A change id
is stable across amends, so jj moves its own bookmark with no force flag and no error:

```
bookmark: push-slxllnxlmxwz [move sideways from b7e44fc98f79 to 8f82f551ad69]
```

Don't re-investigate that half.

**Pros:** a shared remote stays legible.

**Cons:** this is jj's OWN behaviour for an anonymous push, not something Workroom invented — bare
`jj git push --change` does exactly this. Diverging from it means inventing a naming or cleanup policy
that jj users won't expect from other jj tools. Doing nothing is defensible.

**Context / how to start:** `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision` and the `--change` push path; the options are
(a) leave it and document it, (b) offer cleanup of merged `push-*` bookmarks, or (c) require a bookmark
before pushing, which costs the one-click Publish a fresh workroom currently gets.

**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (jj projects only; cosmetic on a personal remote, untidy on a shared one — and the
status quo matches jj's own).

Three commits on `joel/vcs-toolbar`, tree clean. The QA pass is **partly done, and I hit a wall** — reporting both halves.

**Verified against real git**

- **Host-key copy fires correctly.** Real git prints `Host key verification failed.` as the *first* line, then buries it under the generic `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` I'd have been suspicious of that (the classifier could easily have matched the generic line instead), but the first line is what `classify` keys on, and the existing unit-test fixture uses that exact two-line string. Real behaviour matches the test.
- **Lock copy** — verified earlier, both git wordings.
- **Push/pull against a real remote** — covered by the integration suite over `file://`, including the new lock case.

**One gap I could not close: `.authRequired`.** GitHub answers a nonexistent repo with `Repository not found` before any credential exchange, so I couldn't produce a genuine 401 without a real private repo. The classifier keys on git's documented `terminal prompts disabled` / `could not read Username`, which I could not observe live. Its *unit* coverage is real; its trigger against a live server is still unconfirmed. That's the one item on the plan's verification list I'd still want a human to hit once.

Also noted: an unreachable host (DNS failure) falls through to `.other` with git's generic `Could not read from remote repository` — correct but unhelpful. Not worth a case of its own, but it's what a typo'd remote will show.

**Where I stopped: the resize ladder (260→520).** I tried to pin the inspector width by writing `inspector.width` into the throwaway HOME's plist, since launch args can't set a typed `Defaults` key. The app then launched **windowless** — and it now does so even with a clean HOME, though the same command produced windows four times earlier this session. One instance, no crash log. That matches the recorded pattern where many test launches degrade the login session's automation/window subsystem; the recorded remedy is a log out/in, not a code fix.

So the two remaining verification items both need you at the machine:

1. **Resize the inspector 260→520** — check the caption drops before the staleness line, no horizontal scroll, height stays 36pt.
2. **Hover the three segments with a real mouse** — this codebase has bitten twice on hover bugs that synthetic events can't reproduce, so I can't substitute for it at all.
